2.  While scrutinizing these Orders, the Committee note d that there was a considerable time 
lag between issue  of Notifications and their layin g in some cases. The annexed statement also 
indicates the period of delay in cases where Notifi cations have not been laid as per the time 
schedule prescribed by the Committee. The Committee  observed that out of the total 117 delayed 
Notifications, there were 110 Notifications where n o delay statement was appended to. However, 
the bulk of delayed Notifications were from the Ministry of  Road Transport and Highways which 
comes to around 54.7% of the total delayed Notifications. 
 
The observations/recommendations of the Committee i n respect of the specific 
Ministries/Departments where delay in laying of Notifications has been noticed, are as follows: -  
 

 
(i)  Ministry of Communications and Information Technology 
 (Department of Telecommunications) 
 
The Ministry of Communications and Information Tech nology (Department of 
Telecommunications) have laid 4 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 25 – 28). Out of these, 2 Notifications 
have been  delayed by 4 to 6 months. There is no de lay statement appended to one Notification 
(Sl. No. 27) although the other Notification has a delay statement appended (Sl. No. 26) to it. The 
reason for delay given by the Ministry is as under:- 
  
 “The TRAI Regulation No. 2/2016 – Prohibition of D iscriminatory Tariffs for Data 
Services Regulations, 2016 dated the 8 
th  February, 2016 could not be laid down on 13 th  May, 
2016 on the table of Rajya Sabha due to the decisio n taken in the leaders meeting with the 
Hon’ble Chairman on 12 th  May, 2016 that no other business would be transacted.” 
 
 The reason of delay given in case of one Notificat ion by the Ministry is acceptable. 
But in so far as the one where no reason has been a ssigned, the Committee hopes that the 
Ministry would avoid such instances of delay in lay ing of subordinate legislation in future 
and would keep off situations, intentional or unint entional, causing delay. The Committee 
expects them to keep more vigil to avoid such unreasonable delays in future. 
 

 
(ii) Ministry of Corporate Affairs 
 
 The Ministry of Corporate Affairs have laid 21 Not ifications (Sl. Nos. 32 to 52). Out of 
these, one Notification (Sl. No. 41) has been delay ed by 4 months with delay statement appended 
thereto. The reason for delay given by the Ministry is as under:- 
 
 “The Notification relating to the G.S.R. No. 397 ( E), dated 04.04.2016 on the Companies 
(Filing of Documents and Forms in Extensible Business Reporting Language) Amendment Rules, 
2016, was required to be laid before both the House s of Parliament during the Budget Session, 
2016. 
 The above Notification G.S.R. No. 397 (E) dated 04 .04.2016 on the Companies (Filing of 
Documents and Forms in Extensible Business Reporting Language) Amendment Rules, 2016 was 
sent to Government Press for printing. The said not ification could not be laid before both the 
Houses of Parliament during budget Session of the P arliament, 2016 due to delay in receiving the 
Gazette copy of the said notification by this Minis try and when it was collected, the Rajya Sabha 
session was over on 10.05.2016 and Lok Sabha on 13. 05.2016. The said notification got delayed 
and hence it may kindly be condoned.” 
 
 The reason furnished by the Ministry is unacceptab le. This is becoming a recurring 
feature in the responses by the Ministries. The Com mittee have time and again pointed out 

that delay in receiving printing copies of Notifications from the Government Press, is a lame 
excuse. Ministry of Corporate Affairs should plan b eforehand that ample time is given to 
printing press  so that printed copies are received  timely. The Committee suggests the 
Ministry of Corporate Affairs to take adequate prec aution to avoid such delay in future. In 
this regard Committee wants to draw the attention o f the Ministry to its 213 th  Report the 
Committee directs all the Ministries that in case t here is a delay in procuring printed copies 
in time, they may obtain G.S.R. and S.O. numbers fr om the Government of India Press and 
prepare requisite number of copies in cyclostyled f orm for laying in the Parliament. This 
had been even suggested by the controlling Ministry  (Urban Development) of Government 
of India Press so as to avoid such unwanted delays. 
 
(iii) Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate C hange 
 
The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Cha nge have laid 9 Notifications (Sl. 
Nos. 56 to 64) on the Table of the House during the  Session. Out of these, 3 Notifications  (Sl. 
Nos. 61 to 63) have been delayed. The delay period is of about 4 months in each case and, 
moreover, no delay statement has been attached to any of these delayed Notifications.  
 
The Committee takes a strong view of the delay occu rred in tabling the Notifications 
in time and emphasise that the Ministry should avoi d such instances of delay in laying of 
Subordinate Legislation in future. The Committee al so impresses upon the Ministry to take 

note of the fact that in case, there is a delay in the laying of any Statutory Notifications, the 
same should be accompanied by a delay statement whi le it is being laid. The Ministry may 
clarify the reasons for delay in laying and also wh y the delay statement has not been 
appended to the Notifications. 
 
  
(iv) Ministry of Finance (Department of Economic Af fairs) 
 
 The Ministry of Finance (Department of Economic Af fairs) have laid 50 Notifications (Sl. 
Nos. 66 to 115).  Out of these. 36 Notifications (S l. Nos. 73 – 108) have been  delayed by 5 
months to 15 months. There is no delay statement appended to any of these delayed Notifications. 
 
This Committee regrets to say that there is delay i n laying of more than  70% of the 
total Notifications that the Ministry of Finance (Department of Economic Affairs) have laid. 
Further, 10 Notifications have a delay period of mo re than one year and  9 Notifications 
have delay period of more than eleven months. This is not comprehensible to the Committee 
for it is left pondering as to what caused this ino rdinate delay. Furthermore, there is no 
delay statement appended to any of these delayed No tifications. No delay statement coupled  
with inordinate delay is quite enigmatic to the Com mittee. The Committee makes a point 
that Ministry should have appended a delay statement so as to apprise the Parliament of the 
reasons of delay in laying of Notifications on the Table of the House. However, the  Ministry 

of Finance (Department of Economic Affairs) should also strive to cut on the excessive delay 
period in laying of the Notifications. 
 
(v) Ministry of Health and Family Welfare 
 (Department of Health and Family Welfare)  
 
 The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (Departm ent of Health and Family Welfare)  
have laid 7 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 224 to 230). Ou t of these, 3 Notifications  (Sl. Nos. 224 to 
226) have been delayed by 7 to 9 months. The  Minis try did not even bother to append a delay 
statement to any of these.  
 
 The Committee is saddened to see that 3 out of 7 No tifications that the Ministry of 
Health and Family Welfare (Department of Health and  Family Welfare) have laid, have 
been delayed. Further, there is no reason assigned for this delay.  This is in contravention of 
Committee’s recommendation given in its 135 Report that Notifications which are delayed 
should invariably be accompanied by a delay stateme nt. The Committee would like the 
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (Department of Health and Family Welfare) to take 
necessary steps to obviate such delays, and, in cas e of delay in laying of Notifications, delay 
statement should invariably be appended to them. 
 
(vi) Ministry of Home Affairs 

  
The Ministry of Home Affairs have laid 20 Notificat ions (Sl. Nos. 231 to 250) and only 3 
of them have been delayed, with delay of 4 months i n each case (Sl. Nos. 240-242) accompanied 
with delay statement. The reasons of delay given by the Ministry is as under:-  
 
“(i) The National Disaster Response Force, Group “B ” Gazetted,   Non-
Combatised Posts Recruitment (Amendment) Rules, 2015   (GSR 54); 
(ii) The National Disaster Response Force, Group “A ” Gazetted,  
 Combatised Posts Recruitment (Amendment) Rules, 20 15 (GSR   55); and  
(iii) The National Disaster Response Force, Group ‘ B’ and Group ‘  C’ 
Non-Gazette, Combatised Posts Recruitment (Amendment)   Rules, 2015 (GSR 56). 
  
 As per sub-section (1) and clause (f) of sub-secti on (2) of section 75 of the Disaster 
Management Act, 2005 (53 of 2005) the said Rules we re framed & published in the Gazette of 
India. As defined in the procedure all Rules or ‘Or ders’ required to be laid before the House 
should be so laid within a period of 15 days after their publication in the Gazette, if the House is 
in Session, and, if the House is not in Session, th e Rules or ‘Orders’  should be laid on the Table 
of the House as soon as possible (but in any case w ithin 15 days) after the Commencement of the 
following session. 

2. However, the extant Rules (GSR 54 to GSR 56) pub lished in the Gazette on 21 st  March, 
2015 could not be laid before both the Houses of Pa rliament in time due to late receipt of the 
Rules from the Press and inadvertent reasons. 
3. The delay in laying the said Notifications befor e the House is deeply regretted and it is 
requested to condone the delay which occurred due to inadvertent reasons.” 
 
 The  Committee notes with regret that the Ministry  of Home Affairs have failed to 
strictly adhere to the time schedule as prescribed in its 131 
st  Report. In so far as the 
procurement of printed copies from Government of In dia Press is concerned, they may 
resort to the recommendation of the Committee given  time and again, by procuring a 
G.S.R./S.O. number from the Government of India Pre ss and lay it. The Committee hopes 
that the Ministry of Home Affairs would put an effe ctive mechanism in place to eliminate 
such delays in future, particularly on account of d elay in receiving printed copies of 
Notifications. The Committee hopes that such delays would not recur in future.  
 
(vii) Ministry of Power 
 
The Ministry of Power have laid 7 Notifications (Sl . Nos. 284 – 290) out of which two of 
them (Sl. Nos. 284-285) have been delayed by 8 to 9  months respectively. Delay statements are 
appended to both of them. The reasons cited by the Ministry for delay is given below:- 
 

“Notifications Nos. 08/01/2015-BBMB, dated 20 th  October, 2015 and 09/01/2015-BBMB, 
dated the 11 th  December, 2015 were issued by Ministry of Power fo r amendment in BBMB 
Rules, 1974 allowing CPSU officials to join BBMB in Board Level Capacity. 
The above Notifications were  published in the Gaze tte of India (Extraordinary) and 
weekly in the month of October, 2015 and December, 2015 respectively and should have been 
laid on the table of House during the Budget Sessio n of Parliament, 2016. However, the same 
could not be laid on the tables of Parliament due t o change in procedure at Government of India 
Press for obtaining copies of official gazette. The  stabilization of the system change from manual 
to digital publication has taken some time.” 
 
The Committee is constrained to note  the lapse on part of the Ministry of Power 
causing such delay and advises the Ministry to take  necessary anticipatory and advanced 
steps so that loopholes are plugged in so as to ensure that such delays do not recur. 
 
(viii) Ministry of Railways 
  
  The Ministry of Railways have laid 4 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 291 to 294). One 
Notification (Sl. No. 293) has been delayed by six months and there is no delay statement 
appended with the Notification. 
 

The Committee desires that the Ministry of Railways  should strictly adhere to the 
time schedule as recommended by it in its 131st Rep ort in laying of the Subordinate 
Legislation before Parliament. The Ministry is remi nded that in case of any delay in laying 
of the Notifications, a delay statement should also invariably be appended therewith so as to 
apprise the Parliament of the real causes for the same. 
 
 
 
 
 (ix) Ministry of Road Transport and Highways 
 
 The Ministry of Road Transport & Highways have lai d 75 Notifications
 on the Table of 
the House during the Session. Out of these, 64 Noti fications have been delayed. None of these 
have delay statements appended thereto and  the delay period ranges from 4 months to 14 months.  
   
 The Committee takes note of the fact that the Mini stry of Road Transport and 
Highways have to lay  a huge volume of Notification s on the table of the House.  The 
Committee, however, finds that the percentage of de layed Notifications, out of total 
Notifications laid, is quite high i.e. as high as o ver 84.7%. This is simply unacceptable. 
Further, the Ministry have not appended any delay s tatement with any of the  delayed 
Notifications/Rules. Ministry of Road Transport and  Highways should look into the matter 

seriously to eliminate recurrence of such delays in  completing the procedural formalities. 
The Committee desires that Ministry of Road Transpo rt and Highways should adhere to 
the time schedule in laying of Notifications as pre scribed in the Committee’s 131 st  Report 
and append a delay statement without fail in case t here is  delay in laying. This has, sort of 
become a matter of routine with this Ministry, its seems. The Ministry has been reminded 
on this issue on umpteen number of times in the pas t. The Ministry may clarify the reasons 
for delay in laying and also why the delay statemen t has not been appended to the 
Notifications. 
 
(x) Ministry of Textiles 
  
 The Ministry of Textiles have laid 2 Notifications  (Sl. Nos. 379 – 380) and one of these 
(Sl. No. 379) has been delayed by 6 months. There i s no delay statement appended to the 
Notification. 
  
The Committee notes with concern the delay in layin g of one of its Notification on 
the Table of the House. The Committee notices  the Ministry of Textiles   had communicated 
the circumstances causing delay in laying of Notifi cation and also to have appended a delay 
statement therefore. But the Committee finds that t he Ministry of Textiles   have not only 
delayed the laying of one Notification but also did  not append any delay statement thereto. 
The Committee, therefore, advises the Ministry   to strictly adhere to the time schedule in 

future in laying of the Notifications and append a delay statement where there is delay in 
laying of Notification on the Table of the House. T he Committee recommends that the 
Ministry may clarify the reasons for delay in layin g and also why the delay statement has 
not been appended to the Notification. 
 
 
 
 
(xi) Ministry of Urban Development 
 
 Ministry of Urban Development have laid 3 Notifica tions (Sl. Nos. 381 – 383) out of 
which one Notification (Sl. No. 382) is delayed by 4 months and  no  delay statement  is attached  
thereto. 
 
 The Committee reiterates its earlier recommendatio n, that in case of delay in laying, 
Notifications should be accompanied with delay stat ement. Attention to recommendation 
contained in 135 
th  Report of the Committee is drawn here. The Ministr y of Urban 
Development should take care so that repetition of such delay is avoided in future. They 
should take such matters of delay very seriously.  
 

 3.   The Committee impresses upon all the Ministrie s/Departments to take immediate steps to 
ensure timely and proper laying of subordinate legi slation. The Committee, accordingly, wishes 
to bring to the notice of all Ministries/Department s of the Government of India, particularly, the 
defaulting ones, the following recommendations, as contained in its 7 th , 131 
st 
, 135 
th 
, 152 
nd  ,   
192 nd  , 201 st  , 212 th  and 213 th  Reports: 
 
 “The Committee desires that for the convenience of  the public and Members, 
Ministries should henceforth send copies of 'order'  duly authenticated by the Ministers 
concerned, incorporating therein all the correction s and amendments issued till date of 
laying such 'orders' instead of laying the uncorrec ted copy along with corrigenda. The 
Committee feels that to obviate any legal or techni cal difficulty, Ministries should examine 
whether there is any necessity of assigning a separ ate G.S.R. No. to a corrigendum at the 
time of its publication in the Gazette and whether such a corrigendum should not be 
published without assigning any G.S.R. No. The Comm ittee would, therefore, like to 
impress upon all Ministries of the Government of In dia that the present practice of laying 
the rules without incorporating corrigenda in the body of the rules is not a healthy one. The 
Committee hopes that the Ministries will ensure sup ply of only corrected copies of the rules 
for laying on the Table so that they depict a true and correct picture and serve the desired 
purpose."

Parliament of the causes of delay. The Committee de sires all Ministries/Departments to

 “In addition to the concern expressed by the Commi ttee over delay in laying of 
Notifications on the Table of the House, the Committee also express their deep concern over 
delay in framing of rules/regulations under differe nt Acts. The Committee in its 47 
th  report 
presented to the House on 14.9.1981 has recommended  that the rule-making process should 
be completed within a period of six months of the c oming into force of an Act. The 
Committee has further recommended that in case a Mi nistry is not able to adhere to this 
time limit, it should seek extension of time for co mpleting the rule-making process. The 
recommendation of the committee reads as follows:- 

 
  “The Committee feels that the rule-making process c ould well have been 
completed within the time limit of six months which  the Committee has laid down for 
making of rules under an Act after coming into forc e of that Act. Where however, a 
Ministry does not find it possible to adhere to the  time limit, they should inform the 
Committee of the reasons why they cannot make rules  within the time limit and seek 
extension of time for completing the rule-making process.” 
 The Committee is constrained to take note of the f act that the 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India are n ot complying with the Committee’s 
recommendation to complete the process of framing of subordinate legislation contemplated 
under various Acts of Parliament within a period of  six months. At the same time, the 
Committee also does not receive requests for extens ion of time for completing the rule-
making process in terms of its recommendations as a bove from most of the 
Ministries/Departments. The Committee takes a serio us note of the prevailing situation in 
which the Ministries/Departments are neither able t o complete the task of framing 
rules/regulations under different Acts within the g iven six months’ period nor do they suo-
motu  approach the Committee for seeking extension of ti me. The Committee further notes 
that in order to ensure timely framing of rules/reg ulations it has taken an initiative to 
monitor the progress of framing of subordinate legi slation in respect of all legislations 
brought about by different Ministries/Departments o f Government of India from the year 
2003 onwards with a view to ensure that the framing  of subordinate legislation is not 

delayed. The Committee, however, finds that the res ponses from the 
Ministries/Departments have not been prompt in this  monitoring exercise undertaken on 
behalf of the Committee. 
  
 In view of the above position, the Committee once again reiterates its 
recommendation that the Ministries/Departments shou ld ensure putting in place 
subordinate legislation positively within a period of six months of coming into force of the 
Act. The Committee further recommends that in case the Ministry fails to meet with this 
deadline, they should invariably approach the Committee for seeking extension of time. The 
Committee further recommends that in cases where th e time limit of six months is not 
adhered to, they should, while laying rules/regulat ions before the Parliament invariably lay 
a statement explaining the reasons why the framing of rules/regulations was delayed beyond 
six months so as to keep the Parliament apprised of  the compliance of the Parliament’s 
mandate  conferred upon the Executive.”

  Rules/Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are laid by dif ferent Ministries on the Table of 
the House under various provisions of parent Acts p assed by Parliament. These Rules/ 
Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are published in the of ficial Gazette before being laid on the 
Table of the House. Even after they are laid, it is  very difficult to get access to these 

Notifications. The Committee recommends that such R ules/Regulations/Orders, etc. laid on 
the Table of the House should be invariably uploade d on the websites of respective 
Ministries immediately on the same day when they ha ve been laid on the Table of the 
House, for information of Members of Parliament and people at large for their easy access. 
201 st  Report 
(Presented on 14 th  December, 2012)  
 
 
The Committee observes that the whole process of en acting laws is defeated if rules 
are not framed and laid on the Table of the House i n time.  A reasonable delay could be 
understood but unjustifiably long delays should be avoided and the Ministries should work 
towards improving this position.   The Committee hopes that Ministry would strive to k eep 
the delay to the minimum and take care that Notific ations are laid on the Table of the 
House at the first available opportunity after publication of Notifications. 
  
 
The Committee would like to impress upon the Minist ry that it is their responsibility 
to ensure that copies of the Notifications are prin ted timely and for this purpose, they need 
to evolve a suitable mechanism to ensure that notifications are laid in time.   The Committee 
is happy that the Ministry has evolved an internal mechanism/ procedure for this purpose.  

The Committee hopes that it would take action accor dingly in order to comply with the 
prescribed schedule in the matter of laying of statutory Notifications. 
 
The Ministry must take appropriate step to remove l acuna, if any, administrative or 
otherwise, causing such long delay by being little proactive and prompt.  Further, the 
Ministries should take it up with the Ministry of U rban Development for late receiving of 
printed copies of the Notification.

INTRODUCTION 
 
1. I, the Chairperson of the Committee on Subordina te Legislation, having been 
authorized by the Committee, do hereby present on i ts behalf, this Two Hundred and Thirty 
First Report of the Committee.  
 
2.  The Committee examined the matters that came up  while scrutinizing the Khadi and 
Village Industries Commission Regulations, 2007 and  issues relating to them along with the 
comments received from the Government. The Committe e also took into consideration the 
status of implementation of its recommendations as contained in its 220 
th  Report on the 
Framing of Rules and Regulations under the National  Trust for Welfare of Persons With 
Autism, Cerebral Palsy, Mental Retardation and Multiple Disabilities Act, 1999. 
 
3.   The observations and recommendations of the Co mmittee are contained in the 
Report.  
 
4.  The Committee considered and adopted the draft Re port in i 
ts meeting held on the       
28 th   March, 2017. 
 
 
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY  
Chairman  
Committee on Subordinate Legislation,  
 Rajya Sabha

April  10, 2017

KVIC-Khadi and Village Industries Commission 
CPF-Contributory Provident Fund 
MSME-Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises 
 
 
 
  

(i)  REPORT ON  
THE KHADI AND VILLAGE INDUSTRIES COMMISSION 
REGULATIONS, 2007 
  
I.  BACKGROUND 
 
The Khadi and Village Industries Commission Regulat ions, 2007 
(Annexure-I)  were framed in supersession of the Khadi and Villa ge Industries 
Commission Regulations, 1958, in exercise of powers  conferred by Section 27 of 
the Khadi and Village Industries Commission Act, 19 56. The Regulations were 
taken up for detailed examination by the Committee and a questionnaire on the 
subject was forwarded to the Ministry of Micro, Sma ll and Medium Enterprises 
for their comments/clarifications on the 2 nd  December, 2008. After repeated 
reminders, the Ministry furnished their replies on the 17 th  May, 2010 (Annexure-
II) . During the course of its examination, the Committ ee also had discussion with 
the representatives of Khadi and Village Industries  Commission (KVIC), State 
Government of Uttar Pradesh along with the Ministry  of Micro, Small & Medium 
Enterprises at Lucknow on 14 th  June 2015. Study note on the said study visit is 
enclosed as Annexure-III .  
 
2. The Committee enquired about the reasons that ne cessitated the framing of 
the Khadi and Village Industries Commission Regulat ions, 2007, in supersession 
of the Khadi and Village Industries Commission Regu lations, 1958. The Ministry 
of MSME  replied that with a view to revamp the str ucture and functioning of 
KVIC, the Government had constituted an Expert Comm ittee in December 2004 
to recommend suitable measures for revamping of KVI C after reviewing its 
structure, functioning and performance. Based on th e recommendations of the 
Expert Committee, KVIC (Amendment) Bill, 2005 to am end the KVIC Act, 1956 
was drafted and introduced in the Lok Sabha on 22 
nd  August, 2005. Finally, the 
KVIC (Amendment) Bill, 2005 as passed by both House s of Parliament, after 
receiving the assent of the President in March 2006 , became an Act of Parliament 
and the amended provisions came into force with effect from 15 th  May, 2006. 

 
3. Consequent upon the amendment to KVIC Act, 1956 and KVIC Rules, 
2006, many of the provisions of the existing KVIC R egulations 1958 became 
outdated and there was a necessity to suitably amen d the then existing KVIC 
Regulations, 1958. Accordingly, the Government of I ndia, in supersession of the 
KVIC Regulations 1958, notified the KVIC Regulation s, 2007 in the Gazette of 
India on the 31 
st  October, 2007.  
  
II  EXAMINATION OF REGULATIONS, OBSERVATIONS AND 
RECOMMENDATIONS  
 
4. In response to the important points/ issues rais ed by the Committee 
through a detailed questionnaire and discussion wit h the   representatives of the 
Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC), the  Ministry of Micro, Small 
& Medium Enterprises etc., the Ministry has furnish ed their comments/ 
clarifications which are elaborated in the succeedi ng paragraphs along with the 
observations/ recommendations of the Committee. 
 
5. Regulation 3(7) provides that Commission may grant study leave to i ts 
employees in order to enable them to undertake stud y or research or to obtain 
specialized training in scientific, technical or ec onomic subjects connected with 
the work of the Commission, subject to such terms a nd conditions as may be 
prescribed by the Commission. The Committee enquire d from the Ministry how 
many employees have been granted study leave within  the last 4-5 years, in what 
fields and in what way the Commission has been bene fited from such study 
leaves. The Ministry replied that KVIC has reported  that no such study leave has 
been granted during the last 4-5 years by exercisin g the provisions of Regulation 
3(7). The Committee observes that the power to frame the terms and 
conditions to grant study leave to its employees un der the Regulation 3(7) 
have been further delegated. The Committee is of th e view that under the 
power given by this Act to frame regulation on give n items cannot be further 
delegated. These terms and conditions should have b een included in the 

Regulations itself. Therefore, the Committee recomm ends that the terms and 
conditions for granting of study leave should be fr amed by the Commission 
and included in the Regulations itself . 
 
6. Regulation 3(8) provides that the Commission may, with the prior 
approval of Government, make regulations regarding  grant of gratuity, medical 
aid, contributory provident fund, conduct, discipli ne and appeals, etc. The 
Committee enquired about the status of framing of r egulations on these fields. 
The Ministry replied that existing (i) KVIC Employe es (Gratuity) Regulations, 
1975; (ii) KVIC Employees (Medical Attendance) Regu lations, 1961 and (iii) 
KVIC Employees (CPF) Regulations, 1958, which were framed as per the KVIC 
Regulations, 1958 are under revision. The Committee notes that Section 27 (2) 
(a) empowers the Commission to frame Regulations re garding the terms and 
conditions of appointment and service and scales of  pay of officers and 
servants of the Commission. The Committee, however,  notes that instead of 
providing details regarding grant of gratuity, medi cal aid, contributory 
provident fund, conduct, discipline and appeals, et c, Regulation 3(8) simple 
states that the Commission may, with the prior appr oval of the Government 
make regulations on these issues. The Committee is of the view that these 
details should be provided for in the KVIC Regulati ons, 2007 itself as 
mandated by the Act.  The Committee, accordingly, r ecommends that 
Regulation 3(8) should be made more detailed and al l matters delegated 
under it should be provided in the Regulations itself.  
 
7. Regulation 4(3) provides that  the Commission may, by order in writing, 
waive the condition regarding the production of hea lth certificate, within one 
month from date of appointment, altogether in speci al cases if it deems it 
necessary to do so in the interest of the work of t he Commission. The Committee 
pointed out that it should be specified as to what could be the special cases 
wherein a condition for production of health certif icate will be waived and what 
interest it would serve for the Commission. Ministr y replied that practically no 

relaxation is granted by the KVIC in the production  of health certificate and that 
this provision is required to be suitably modified in consultation with KVIC and 
accordingly, action will be taken . The Committee notes the reply of the 
Ministry that practically no relaxation is granted by KVIC for production of 
health certificate and, accordingly, recommends that the provision for waiver 
of production of health certificate should be deleted from these Regulations.  
 
8. Regulation 23 provides that  the Commission may delegate necessary 
financial powers to its officers for ensuring exped itious disposal of work and 
smooth and efficient functioning of the organizatio n and that the Commission 
may make suitable rules in this behalf for the guid ance of its staff in order to 
ensure that these powers are judiciously used by th e officers concerned. The 
Committee notes that Section 27(2)(c) empowers the Commission to frame 
regulations regarding the delegation of powers and duties to any employee of 
the Commission. The Committee, however, notes that Regulation 23 has 
further delegated powers to the Commission to frame  rules for judicious use 
of financial powers by officers of the Commission w ithout providing the 
details in the Regulations itself. The Committee, t herefore, recommends that 
Regulation 23 should be made more detailed by inclu ding the rules for 
judicious use of financial powers by the officers o f the Commission in the 
Regulations itself.  
 
9. Regulation 24 (1) provides that the Commission shall appoint one or 
more 
Certification Committees which shall grant certific ates to producers of, or dealers 
in khadi or the products of any village industry an d Regulation 24(2)  provides that a 
Certification Committee shall consist of such numbe r of members as the 
Commission may think fit to appoint thereto, and on e of them shall be appointed 
as the Chairman of the Committee. The Committee, however, notes that the 
number of members, the manner/procedure of appointm ent of members of 
the Central Certification Committees and Zonal Cert ification Committees, 
the qualification, experience, etc of the members should have been prescribed 

in the Regulations. The Committee, accordingly, rec ommends that the 
number of members of the Certification Committee, t he manner/procedure 
of appointment, the qualifications, experience, etc should be prescribed in the 
Regulations itself. 
 
III SUMMARY OF THE OBSERVATIONS / RECOMMENDATIONS  
OF THE COMMITTEE  
 
Regulation 3(7) 
 
10. The Committee observes that the power to frame the terms and 
conditions to grant study leave to its employees un der the Regulation 3(7) 
have been further delegated. The Committee is of th e view that under the 
power given by this Act to frame regulation on give n items cannot be further 
delegated. These terms and conditions should have b een included in the 
Regulations itself. Therefore, the Committee recomm ends that the terms and 
conditions for granting of study leave should be fr amed by the Commission 
and included in the Regulations itself . 
 
Regulation 3(8) 
11. The Committee notes that Section 27 (2) (a) emp owers the 
Commission to frame Regulations regarding the terms  and conditions of 
appointment and service and scales of pay of office rs and servants of the 
Commission. The Committee, however, notes that inst ead of providing 
details regarding grant of gratuity, medical aid, contributory provident fund, 
conduct, discipline and appeals, etc, Regulation 3( 8) simple states that the 
Commission may, with the prior approval of the Gove rnment make 
regulations on these issues. The Committee is of th e view that these details 
should be provided for in the KVIC Regulations, 200 7 itself as mandated by 
the Act.  The Committee, accordingly, recommends th at Regulation 3(8)

provided in the Regulations itself.  
 

Regulation 4(3) 
12. The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry t hat practically no 
relaxation is granted by KVIC for production of hea lth certificate and,

Regulation 23  
13. The Committee notes that Section 27(2)(c) empow ers the Commission 
to frame regulations regarding the delegation of po wers and duties to any 
employee of the Commission. The Committee, however,  notes that 
Regulation 23 has further delegated powers to the C ommission to frame 
rules for judicious use of financial powers by offi cers of the Commission 
without providing the details in the Regulations it self. The Committee, 
therefore, recommends that Regulation 23 should be made more detailed by 
including the rules for judicious use of financial powers by the officers of the

Regulation 24 (1) and 24(2)

Report  
On  
The framing of Rules & Regulations under the National Trust for Welfare of Persons with 
Autism, Cerebral Palsy, Mental Retardation and Multiple Disabilities Act, 1999- 
Implementation of the 220 th  Report of the Committee on Subordinate Legislation, Rajya 
Sabha. 
 The Committee took up for consideration the status  of framing of rules/regulations under 
the National Trust for Welfare of Persons with Auti sm, Cerebral Palsy, Mental Retardation and 
Multiple Disabilities Act, 1999. During the course of examination the Committee observed a 
number of discrepancies in the framing of rules and  regulations and accordingly presented its 
220 th  Report on the subject to the Rajya Sabha on 18 th  December, 2014. 
2. The Committee had inter-alia given the following  recommendations: 
“23.        The Committee is pained to find that se nsitivity shown by Parliament to 
have made a pioneering law to provide much needed h elp and succour to the most 
vulnerable and needy sections of our society is bei ng dealt in the most insensitive 
and callous manner.  The manner in which this law i s being implemented leaves 
much to be desired.  The absence of specific guidel ines, rules, regulations, etc. on 
various aspects for enforcing the Act as per its le tter and spirit, has bred to secrecy, 
scope for discretion and hence lack of transparency  in the working of National 
Trust.  Thus, the Ministry due to reasons best know n to it, failed to perform its 
responsibility as an administrative controller as i t did not carefully see that all the 
Guidelines, Rules and Regulations have been framed.   More serious thing is that 
the Ministry, it appears, did not consult Legislati ve Department in vetting the 
Rules, Regulations as is usually done by all the Mi nistries.  Had it been done so, 
much of the problems pointed out by the Committee n ow may not have arisen at 
all.   
24.  The Committee re-emphasizes that the Ministry should expedite framing 
the Recruitment Rules not only for the post of Chai rman, National Trust but also 
for the officers and employees of the National Trust at the earliest. The Committee 
is of the view that this process can be completed i n a fixed time schedule given 
that much ground work on the educational qualifications and experience required 
for the said post has already been done with help o f DOPT.  Even the suggestions 
of the DoPT have not been properly ingrained into t he existing criteria.  Further, 
notifying the Rules would give the candidates an op portunity to know the 
requirements for the requisite post apart from givi ng publicity to the working of 
the National Trust. 
 
25. The Committee recommends that the Ministry shou ld re-visit the 
Rules/Regulations framed under the National Trust f or Welfare of Persons with 
Autism, Cerebral Palsy, Mental Retardation and Mult iple Disabilities Act, 1999 

and re-examine them in the light of the observation s made by the Committee in 
the preceding paragraphs and effect necessary modifications as needed. 
 
26. The Committee further recommends that the Minis try may look into the 
possibility of increasing the Corpus Fund of the Na tional Trust. In Committee’s 
view, lack of adequate funding should not be a limi ting factor for the working of 
the National Trust for fulfilling its mandate.  Inc reased corpus is needed urgently 
keeping in view the enhanced coverage of the scheme s being operated by the 
National Trust.  
 
 27.  The Committee is hopeful that the Ministry wo uld carry out the 
recommendations of the Committee expeditiously unde r intimation to it. The 
Committee would further like to impress upon the Ministry that proper monitoring 
and inspection are essential for the proper and eff ective implementation of Rules 
and Regulations, and, stresses upon the Ministry to  strengthen its enforcement 
mechanism to ensure that the objectives of the Order are achieved.” 
 
3. The Report was forwarded to the Ministry of Soci al Justice & Empowerment 
(Department of Disability Affairs) on 22 
nd  December, 2014 for information and immediate 
necessary action. The Ministry submitted its interi m Action Taken Note on 12 th  March, 2015 
(Annexure I) . Ministry was thereafter again requested vide  this Secretariat Office Memorandum 
dated the 22 nd  May, 2015 to furnish the status of implementation of the 220 th  Report of the 
Committee with special reference to revision of the Rules/Regulations framed under the National 
Trust Act, 1999 and to furnish a detailed note on t he status of ARUNIM regarding its legal 
status. The Ministry furnished final Action Taken N ote on  8th  June, 2015 (Annexure II). The 
comments/clarifications furnished by the Ministry w ith regard to the recommendations of the 
Committee as contained in its 220th Report are reproduced in the succeeding paragraphs. 
 
4. The Committee had recommended that the Ministry should, without any further delay, 
frame guidelines with details regarding the basic q ualifications including educational 
qualifications and experience along with the proced ure for appointment of the Chairperson, 
National Trust.  
 
5.  In response the Ministry informed that they had  amended the National Trust Rules to 
incorporate educational qualifications, selection p rocedure for appointment of Chairperson, 
National Trust vide  Notification No. G.S.R. 7(E) dated 4 
th  February, 2015.  
 

6. The Committee notes with satisfaction that the M inistry has taken prompt action on its 
recommendation regarding basic qualifications inclu ding educational qualifications and 
experience along with the procedure for appointment  of the Chairperson, National Trust. The 
Committee wishes that the Ministry has ensured that  the intent of the Committee as expressed 
through this  recommendation has been properly incorporated in the amendments made in the 
National Trust Rules. 
  
7. As regards the Committee’s observation and recom mendation that the words “ or until his 
successor shall have been duly appointed, whichever  is longer” may be deleted by bringing an 
amendment in Section 4(1) of the Act, the Ministry informed that issue of amending Section 4(1) 
of the National Trust Act, 1999 has been taken up w ith the Ministry of Law & Justice and its 
opinion was awaited.  
 
8. The Committee took note of the Ministry’s commen t that the recommendation 
regarding amendment of Section 4(1) of the Act had been taken up with the Ministry of Law & 
Justice.  The Committee, however, is of the opinion that the Ministry instead of dragging it for 
such a long time should have amended the section by  now, to incorporate the views of the 
Committee.  The Committee, accordingly, directs the  Ministry to expedite the process of 
amendment of the Act in accordance with the letter and spirit with which the Committee had 
made the recommendation. This was the most abused s ection of the Act about which 
Committee had expressed a strong opinion.    
 
9. The Committee  noted  that  as regards  its  recomme ndations on  the  issues   
pertaining to  (i) framing of Rules clarifying the procedure for selection of the Board 
Members other than ex-officio including re-nominati on and removal of Members; (ii) re-
examination of the Regulations 4(4) and 4(5) for ir oning out any discrepancies in the 
subordinate legislation framed by the National Trus t/ Ministry; and (iii) 
 redrafting of  
Regulations7(1) and 8(1) & (2) to avoid further del egation of power, the Ministry had set up a 
Committee headed by the Secretary, Department of Em powerment of Persons with Disabilities 
to review the Rules/ Regulations under the National  Trust Act, 1999 and the Committee held 
its first meeting on 22 nd  April, 2015.  

 
10. The Committee appreciates the Ministry for its promptness in setting up the committee 
under the chairmanship of Secretary, Department of Empowerment of Persons with 
Disabilities to look into its recommendations.   Ho wever, as per the information supplied the 
Committee observes that since the formation of said  committee only one meeting was held on 
22 
nd  April, 2015 wherein  some broad decisions were tak en on the issues raised by the 
Committee. The Committee takes serious note of the fact that since then almost two years have 
elapsed and the Ministry till date has not bothered  to approach the Committee to inform it 
about the status on these issues. The Committee fee ls that since these rules/regulations have 
not been amended, in effect it means that during th is period the existing  rules about which 
the Committee recorded its observations are being i mplemented. The Committee wants to 
know the status of the Rules/ Regulations on the sa id issues and expects the Ministry to 
intimate it of the same at the earliest.  The Commi ttee further hopes that the Committee set up 
by the Ministry has taken into consideration all as pects upon which the Committee had 
dwelled in its 220 th  Report on the matter, and, accordingly modify the rules/regulations.  
 
11. The Committee observed that its recommendation regarding looking into the possibility 
of increasing the Corpus Fund of the National Trust  was not accepted by the Ministry of 
Social Justice & Empowerment as the Ministry of Fin ance turned down the proposal. The 
Committee, however, was satisfied that the Finance Ministry was considering to provide 
financial/ budgetary support to the flagship scheme s of the National Trust to enhance its 
activities.   Committee’s main concern is that lack  of adequate funding should not be a 
limiting factor for the working of the National Tru st for fulfilling its mandate and hopes that 
the newly granted budgetary fund would provide the adequate financial support to the 
National Trust through its flagship schemes and enhance it’s activities.       
 
12. On the issue of ARUNIM, the Committee notes the obs ervation of the Board of 
National Trust that the Association for Rehabilitat ion under National Trust Initiative 
Marketing (ARUNIM) was technically an organization not a scheme and it should be 
registered with the Trust for funds. As per decisio n taken by Board ARUNIM became a 
registered organization of National Trust and conse quently no financial support was given to 

them during 2014-15. ARUNIM also refunded balance f und which was unutilized by the 
Trust. The Committee expresses its concern over the  association of ARUNIM with the 
National Trust without getting it registered with it as it was organization and not a scheme and 
recommends that the Ministry should, in future, ens ure that proper safeguards are installed to 
ensure that such organizations are associated with it by following the proper procedures. 
 
13. Further, the Committee is not satisfied by the Note containing information 
regarding the setting up and later disbanding the o rganisation called ARUNIM within the 
National Trust, the Committee would like to term it  as fiasco committed by the over-
enthusiasm of the persons who failed to observe est ablished procedures. How could they go 
on allocating funds during 2008-2014 without any cl ue about its utilization and 
achievement for which it was set up. Merely refunding a part of the amount out of the more 
than Rs two crore given, does not absolve the perso ns of their responsibility. The 
Committee in view of the manner ARUNIM fiasco has h appened is constrained to 
recommend that it needs to be enquired further and responsibility fixed. The entire 
exercise needs to be completed within two months and report be furnished to be Committee 
for consideration.  
14. The Committee deliberating on Recruitment Rules als o emphasized that the 
Ministry should expedite framing of Recruitment Rul es not only for post of Chairman, 
National Trust but also for the Officers and employ ees of the Trust at the earliest. The 
Ministry in their reply stated that as regard to Re cruitment Rules for other employees, the 
necessary action to framing of Recruitment Rules is being taken by the National Trust. The 
Committee takes serious view of the fact that even after lapse of almost one and half years 
Ministry did not bother to inform the Committee of the steps taken by the Trust in this 
regard. The Committee expects that the Ministry sho uld take pro-active role and 
accordingly impress upon the Trust to frame the Rec ruitment Rules for the employees on 
priority basis and accordingly inform the Committee.   
 
15. The Committee is hopeful that the Ministry will car ry out the recommendations of the 
Committee expeditiously under intimation to it. The  Committee is also of the opinion that 
proper safeguards are essential for giving effect t o the spirit with which the Parliament passed 

the  National Trust for Welfare of Persons with Autism, Cerebral Palsy, Mental Retardation 
and Multiple Disabilities Act, 1999 and stresses up on the Ministry to ensure that the benefits 
incorporated in the Act reach the intended recipients.

2.  While scrutinizing these Orders, the Committee note d that there was a considerable time

schedule prescribed by the Committee. The Committee  observed that out of the total 150 delayed

th  Report that delay

concrete steps to ensure timely and proper laying o f subordinate legislation. The Committee, 
accordingly, wishes to bring to the notice of all M inistries/Departments of the Government of 
India, particularly, the defaulting ones, the follo wing recommendations, as contained in its 7 
th ,

st 
, 135 
th

 “The Committee desires that for the convenience of  the public and Members, 
Ministries should henceforth send copies of 'order'  duly authenticated by the Ministers 
concerned, incorporating therein all the correction s and amendments issued till date of 
laying such 'orders' instead of laying the uncorrec ted copy along with corrigenda. The 
Committee feels that to obviate any legal or techni cal difficulty, Ministries should examine 
whether there is any necessity of assigning a separ ate G.S.R. No. to a corrigendum at the 
time of its publication in the Gazette and whether such a corrigendum should not be 
published without assigning any G.S.R. No. The Comm ittee would, therefore, like to 
impress upon all Ministries of the Government of In dia that the present practice of laying 
the rules without incorporating corrigenda in the body of the rules is not a healthy one. The 

Committee hopes that the Ministries will ensure sup ply of only corrected copies of the rules 
for laying on the Table so that they depict a true and correct picture and serve the desired 
purpose."

 The Committee approve the following draft revised f ormula for laying of Statutory 
Rules before both Houses of Parliament which the Mi nistry of Law and Justice propose to 
incorporate in all future legislation which provide  for making of rules by the 
CentralGovernment:— 
 
 "Every rule made by the Central Government under t his Act shall be laid, as soon as 
may be after it is made, before each House of Parli ament, while it is in session, for a 
total period of thirty days which may be comprised in one session or in two or more 
successive sessions, and if, before the expiry of t he session immediately following the 
session or the successive sessions aforesaid, both Houses agree in making any 
modification in the rule or both Houses agree that the rule should not be made, the rule 
shall thereafter have effect only in such modified form or be of no effect, as the case 
may be; so, however that any such modification or a nnulment shall be without 
prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under that rule." 
  

The Committee recommend that the revised formula sh ould be incorporated not only in 
new legislation but also in the existing Acts as an d when Bills to amend them are brought 
before Parliament. The Ministry should also incorpo rate the new formula in the Bills 
pending before Parliament. This will, in the opinio n of the Committee, bring about 
uniformity in the matter expeditiously. 
(10 th   Report) 
(presented on 24 th  May, 1971) 
 
 “Orders required to be laid before the House shoul d be laid (i) if the House is not in 
Session, during the Session immediately following t he date of publication of the Order in 
the Official Gazette and (ii) if the House is in Se ssion, on the date of the publication of the 
Order, during its continuance and in case the time lag between the date of publication and 
the date of the closing of the Session is less than  15 clear days, before the expiry of the 
Session immediately following the said Session. All  the Ministries/Departments of 
Government of India should henceforth comply with this schedule in the matter of laying of 
the Orders issued under various Acts of Parliament on the Table of the Rajya Sabha.

Parliament of the causes of delay. The Committee de sires all Ministries/Departments to 
take a note of this, since the intention is that th rough the process of formulation of a delay 
statement, the Ministry is able to introspect, iden tify bottlenecks and devise remedial 
measures”.

 “In the opinion of the Committee, every notificati on should be assigned a distinctive

where there are more than one Notifications under a  single file, the Ministries/Departments

nd

 “In addition to the concern expressed by the Commi ttee over delay in laying of 
Notifications on the Table of the House, the Committee also express their deep concern over 
delay in framing of rules/regulations under differe nt Acts. The Committee in its 47 th  report 
presented to the House on 14.9.1981 has recommended  that the rule-making process should 
be completed within a period of six months of the c oming into force of an Act. The 
Committee has further recommended that in case a Mi nistry is not able to adhere to this 
time limit, it should seek extension of time for co mpleting the rule-making process. The 
recommendation of the committee reads as follows:- 
 
  “The Committee feels that the rule-making process c ould well have been 
completed within the time limit of six months which  the Committee has laid down for 
making of rules under an Act after coming into forc e of that Act. Where however, a 
Ministry does not find it possible to adhere to the  time limit, they should inform the 
Committee of the reasons why they cannot make rules  within the time limit and seek 
extension of time for completing the rule-making process.” 
  
 The Committee is constrained to take note of the f act that the 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India are n ot complying with the Committee’s 
recommendation to complete the process of framing of subordinate legislation contemplated 
under various Acts of Parliament within a period of  six months. At the same time, the 
Committee also does not receive requests for extens ion of time for completing the rule-

making process in terms of its recommendations as a bove from most of the 
Ministries/Departments. The Committee takes a serio us note of the prevailing situation in 
which the Ministries/Departments are neither able t o complete the task of framing 
rules/regulations under different Acts within the g iven six months’ period nor do they suo-
motu  approach the Committee for seeking extension of ti me. The Committee further notes 
that in order to ensure timely framing of rules/reg ulations it has taken an initiative to 
monitor the progress of framing of subordinate legi slation in respect of all legislations 
brought about by different Ministries/Departments o f Government of India from the year 
2003 onwards with a view to ensure that the framing  of subordinate legislation is not 
delayed. The Committee, however, finds that the res ponses from the 
Ministries/Departments have not been prompt in this  monitoring exercise undertaken on 
behalf of the Committee. 
  
 In view of the above position, the Committee once again reiterates its 
recommendation that the Ministries/Departments shou ld ensure putting in place 
subordinate legislation positively within a period of six months of coming into force of the 
Act. The Committee further recommends that in case the Ministry fails to meet with this 
deadline, they should invariably approach the Committee for seeking extension of time. The 
Committee further recommends that in cases where th e time limit of six months is not 
adhered to, they should, while laying rules/regulat ions before the Parliament invariably lay 
a statement explaining the reasons why the framing of rules/regulations was delayed beyond 

six months so as to keep the Parliament apprised of  the compliance of the Parliament’s 
mandate  conferred upon the Executive.”

nd 
 Report) 
(Presented on 26 th   August 2011)  
 
  Rules/Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are laid by dif ferent Ministries on the Table of 
the House under various provisions of parent Acts p assed by Parliament. These Rules/ 
Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are published in the of ficial Gazette before being laid on the 
Table of the House. Even after they are laid, it is  very difficult to get access to these 
Notifications. The Committee recommends that such R ules/Regulations/Orders, etc. laid on 
the Table of the House should be invariably uploade d on the websites of respective 
Ministries immediately on the same day when they ha ve been laid on the Table of the 
House, for information of Members of Parliament and people at large for their easy access. 
201 
st  Report 
(Presented on 14 th  December, 2012)  
 
The Committee observes that the whole process of en acting laws is defeated if rules 
are not framed and laid on the Table of the House i n time.  A reasonable delay could be 
understood but unjustifiably long delays should be avoided and the Ministries should work 
towards improving this position.   The Committee hopes that Ministry would strive to k eep 

the delay to the minimum and take care that Notific ations are laid on the Table of the 
House at the first available opportunity after publication of Notifications. 
 
The Committee would like to impress upon the Minist ry that it is their responsibility 
to ensure that copies of the Notifications are prin ted timely and for this purpose, they need 
to evolve a suitable mechanism to ensure that notifications are laid in time.   The Committee 
is happy that the Ministry has evolved an internal mechanism/ procedure for this purpose.  
The Committee hopes that it would take action accor dingly in order to comply with the 
prescribed schedule in the matter of laying of statutory Notifications. 
 
The Ministry must take appropriate step to remove l acuna, if any, administrative or 
otherwise, causing such long delay by being little proactive and prompt.  Further, the 
Ministries should take it up with the Ministry of U rban Development for late receiving of 
printed copies of the Notification. 
212 
th   Report 
(Presented on  3 rd  September, 2013) 
 
 “The Committee is not inclined to accept the late availability of printed copies of 
Notifications from the Government of India Press as  the reason for delay in laying of the 
Notifications. The Committee directs all the Minist ries that in case there is a delay in 
procuring printed copies in time, they may obtain G .S.R. and S.O. numbers from the 

Government of India Press and prepare requisite num ber of copies in cyclostyled form for 
laying in the Parliament. The Committee also recomm ends that this process may be 
adopted by Ministries suo moto  on immediate basis so as to avoid such delays henceforth”.

Report.

DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY

April 10, 2017 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

ACRONYMS
