and accordingly, it is for the Ministry only to ens ure that 
they receive the printed copies  timely.  
The Committee is not inclined to accept the late 
availability of printed copies of Notifications fro m the 
Government of India Press as the reason for delay i n 
laying of the Notifications. The Committee directs all the 
Ministries that, in case, there is delay in procuring printed 
copies in time, they may obtain G.S.R. and S.O. num bers 
from the Government of India Press and prepare 
requisite number of copies in cyclostyled form for laying 

in the Parliament as suggested by Secretary, Minist ry of  
Urban Development, the controlling Ministry of 
Government of India Press, in its meeting held on 3 0  
July, 2013. The Committee also recommends that this  
process may be adopted by Ministries suo moto  on 
immediate basis so as to avoid such delays henceforth. 
 
(viii)  Ministry of Law and Justice 
 (Department of Justice) 
  
The Ministry of Law and Justice (Department of 
Justice)  have laid 3 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 544 t o 546). Two 
of them (Sl. Nos. 544 and 545) have been delayed. T he delay 
period ranges from 24 months to  30 months and are 
accompanied with delay statement to both the delaye d 
Notifications. The reason given by the Ministry for delay is as 
under:-  
 
“The National Legal Services Authority Rules, 1995 
has been amended by way of Notification G.S.R. 75 ( E), 
dated 05.02.2015. The National Legal Services Autho rities 
(Amendment) Rules, 2016 and the National Legal Serv ices 
Authority Rules, 1995 has been amended by way of 
Notification  No. S.O. 2164 (E), dated 12.08.2015. The 
National Legal Services Authorities (Second Amendme nt) 
Rules, 2015 could not be laid before the House of t he 
Parliament, due to administrative reasons.” 
 
The Committee does not accept the reasons of 
delay given by the Ministry of Law and Justice 
(Department of Justice) and expresses its serious c oncern 
over such inordinate delays which ranges from 24 mo nths 
to 30 months. The Committee wonders  how 
administrative procedural process can take 24 to 30  

months to receive Notifications and complete proced ural 
formalities. The Committee feels that Ministry did not 
take adequate precaution to avoid the delay and mad e no 
serious efforts to lay the Notifications in time wh ich is in 
contravention of its statutory obligation to Parlia ment. 
The Committee recommends that the Ministry must tak e 
appropriate steps to remove the lacuna, if any, due  to 
administrative or any other reason causing such lon g 
delay and wish it  would strive to keep delay to th e 
minimum by playing a more proactive role and pursui ng 
with the concerned organisations to act with prompt ness 
in future. 
 
 
(ix) Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas 
 
 The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas have lai d 
3 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 560 to 562). Only 1 Notif ication (Sl. 
No. 560) has been delayed by 5 months and there is no delay 
statement appended to it.  
  
   The Committee is not happy to see that 1 out of 3 
Notifications that the Ministry of Petroleum and Na tural 
Gas have laid, has been delayed and no reason has b een 
given for this delay.  This is in contravention of 
Committee’s recommendation given in its 135 
th   Report 
that Notifications, which are delayed, should invariably be 
accompanied by a delay statement. The Committee wou ld 
like the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas to t ake 
necessary steps to obviate such delays and in case of delay 
in laying of Notifications, delay statements should  
invariably be appended to them. 
  
 

 
(x) Ministry of Road Transport and Highways 
 
 The Ministry of Road Transport & Highways have 
laid 56 Notifications
 on the Table of the House (Sl. Nos. 569 
to 624). A total of  7 Notifications have been dela yed out of 
which 2 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 569 – 570)  are accompanied 
by delay statements and 5 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 5 81 –585)  
have no delay statements appended with them. The de lay 
period ranges from 4 months to 5 months. The reason s given 
by the Ministry is that it took some time to comple te the 
procedural formalities and, therefore, papers could  not be laid 
in time. 
 
The Committee does not accept the reasons of the 
delay given by the Ministry of Road Transport and 
Highways that it took some time to collect the pape rs and 
complete the procedural formalities. The Committee 
wonders how can it take five months to receive 
Notifications and to complete procedural formalitie s. The 
Committee feels that Ministry did not take adequate  
precaution to avoid the delay. The Committee furthe r 
takes a serious view of the fact that even after delay of five 
months in two case Ministry did not feel it necessa ry to 
append a delay statement so as to apprise the Parli ament 
of the reasons for the delay. The Committee recomme nds 
that the Ministry should initiate urgent measures s o as to 
avoid delay in completing the procedural formalitie s so 
that such delay can be eliminated. 
 
 
 
 
(xi)  Ministry of Textiles 

 
 The Ministry of Textiles have laid 2 Notifications  
during the Session (Sl. Nos. 638 to 639). There is only one 
Notification (Sl. No. 538) which was delay by a per iod of 26 
months and a delay statement has been appended ther eto. The 
reasons given by the Ministry are as follows:- 
 
 “The requirement of laying of the Central Silk Boa rd 
(Administrative, Accounts and General Cadre Posts) 
Recruitment Rules, 2015 and corrigendum thereon pub lished 
in Part II – Section 3 – Sub-Section (i) of the Gaz ette of 
Indian Extraordinary Notification dated 11.12.2015 and 
03.06.2016 before the House could not be complied w ith due 
to lack of clarity whether it should be laid in the  House of 
Parliament or otherwise as per Department of Person nel & 
Training’s O.M. No. 14017/48/2010-Estt. (RR) dated 
31.12.2010, hence the delay is regretted.” 
  
 The Committee does not appreciate the reasons 
given by the Ministry of Textiles that Notification s could 
not be laid on the Table of the House due to lack o f 
clarity. This is sheer lackadaisical approach on th e part of 
the Ministry to have neglected the constitutional 
responsibility. This approach calls for 
relook/introspection so as to bring improvement in the 
current situation. 
 The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Textiles 
would avoid such instances of delay in laying of 
subordinate legislation in future and would remove 
lacuna, if any, causing delay. The Committee also a dvises 
the Ministry to avoid recurrence of such delays in future.  
 
3.   The Committee impresses upon all the 
Ministries/Departments to take immediate steps to e nsure 

timely and proper laying of subordinate legislation . The 
Committee, accordingly, wishes to bring to the noti ce of all 
Ministries/Departments of the Government of India, 
particularly, the defaulting ones, the following 
recommendations, as contained in its 131 
st 
, 135 
th 
, 152 
nd 
,   
192 nd ,  201 st ,  212 th  and 213 th  Reports: 
 
 “Orders required to be laid before the House shoul d 
be laid (i) if the House is not in Session, during the Session 
immediately following the date of publication of the Order 
in the Official Gazette and (ii) if the House is in  Session, 
on the date of the publication of the Order, during  its 
continuance and in case the time lag between the da te of 
publication and the date of the closing of the Sess ion is 
less than 15 clear days, before the expiry of the S ession 
immediately following the said Session. All the 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India shoul d 
henceforth comply with this schedule in the matter of 
laying of the Orders issued under various Acts of 
Parliament on the Table of the Rajya Sabha. 
(131 st  Report) 
(Presented on 15 December 2000) 
 
 “The Committee has, time and again, emphasized 
that it is essential that in case there is a delay in the laying 
of Statutory Orders, the concerned Ministry/Departm ent 
should invariably append a delay statement along with the 
Notifications being laid so as to apprise Parliamen t of the 
causes of delay. The Committee desires all 
Ministries/Departments to take a note of this, sinc e the 
intention is that through the process of formulatio n of a 
delay statement, the Ministry is able to introspect, identify 
bottlenecks and devise remedial measures”. 

(135 th  Report) 
(Presented on 27 July 2001) 
 
 “In the opinion of the Committee, every notificati on 
should be assigned a distinctive number in order to  give it 
a separate identity and similarly, no notification should be 
published/laid which does not carry a notification 
number. The Committee expects all 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India to 
exercise caution in this regard. In case where ther e are 
more than one Notifications under a single file, th e 
Ministries/Departments should ensure that the file 
number on each notification should be suitably 
distinguished from one another.” 
(152 
nd 
 Report) 
(Presented on 26 August 2004)  
 
 “In addition to the concern expressed by the 
Committee over delay in laying of Notifications on the 
Table of the House, the Committee also express thei r deep 
concern over delay in framing of rules/regulations under 
different Acts. The Committee in its 47 
th  report presented 
to the House on 14.9.1981 has recommended that the rule-
making process should be completed within a period of six 
months of the coming into force on an Act. The 
Committee has further recommended that in case a 
Ministry is not able to adhere to this time limit, it should 
seek extension of time for completing the rule-maki ng 
process. The recommendation of the committee reads as 
follows:- 
 

  “The Committee feels that the rule-
making process could well have been completed 
within the time limit of six months which the 
Committee has laid down for making of rules 
under an Act after coming into force of that Act. 
Where however, a Ministry does not find it possible 
to adhere to the time limit, they should inform the  
Committee of the reasons why they cannot make 
rules within the time limit and seek extension of 
time for completing the rule-making process.” 
 The Committee is constrained to take note of the 
fact that the Ministries/Departments of Government of 
India are not complying with the Committee’s 
recommendation to complete the process of framing o f 
subordinate legislation contemplated under various Acts 
of Parliament within a period of six months. At the  same 
time, the Committee also does not receive requests for 
extension of time for completing the rule-making pr ocess 
in terms of its recommendations as above from most of 
the Ministries/Departments. The Committee takes a 
serious note of the prevailing situation in which t he 
Ministries/Departments are neither able to complete  the 
task of framing rules/regulations under different A cts 
within the given six months’ period nor do they suo-motu  
approach the Committee for seeking extension of tim e. 
The Committee further notes that in order to ensure  
timely framing of rules/regulations it has taken an  
initiative to monitor the progress of framing of 
subordinate legislation in respect of all legislati ons 
brought about by different Ministries/Departments o f 
Government of India from the year 2003 onwards with  a 
view to ensure that the framing of subordinate legi slation 
is not delayed. The Committee, however, finds that the 

responses from the Ministries/Departments have not been 
prompt in this monitoring exercise undertaken on be half 
of the Committee. 
  
 In view of the above position, the Committee once 
again reiterates its recommendation that the 
Ministries/Departments should ensure putting in pla ce 
subordinate legislation positively within a period of six 
months of coming into force of the Act. The Committ ee 
further recommends that in case the Ministry fails to meet 
with this deadline, they should invariably approach  the 
Committee for seeking extension of time. The Commit tee 
further recommends that in cases where the time lim it of 
six months is not adhered to, they should, while la ying 
rules/regulations before the Parliament invariably lay a 
statement explaining the reasons why the framing of  
rules/regulations was delayed beyond six months so as to 
keep the Parliament apprised of the compliance of t he 
Parliament’s mandate  conferred upon the Executive.” 
(192 
nd 
 Report) 
(Presented on 26 August 2011)  
 
  “Rules/Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are laid by 
different Ministries on the Table of the House unde r 
various provisions of parent Acts passed by Parliam ent. 
These Rules/ Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are publis hed 
in the official Gazette before being laid on the Table of the 
House. Even after they are laid, it is very difficu lt to get 
access to these Notifications. The Committee recomm ends 
that such Rules/Regulations/Orders, etc. laid on th e Table 
of the House should be invariably uploaded on the 
websites of respective Ministries immediately on th e same 
day when they have been laid on the Table of the Ho use, 

for information of Members of Parliament and people  at 
large for their easy access.” 
201 st  Report 
(Presented on 14 th  December, 2012)  
 
 
“The Committee observes that the whole process of 
enacting laws is defeated if rules are not framed a nd laid 
on the Table of the House in time.  A reasonable de lay 
could be understood but unjustifiably long delays s hould 
be avoided and the Ministries should work towards 
improving this position.   The Committee hopes that 
Ministry would strive to keep the delay to the mini mum 
and take care that Notifications are laid on the Ta ble of 
the House at the first available opportunity after 
publication of Notifications. 
  
The Committee would like to impress upon the 
Ministry that it is their responsibility to ensure that copies 
of the Notifications are printed timely and for thi s 
purpose, they need to evolve a suitable mechanism t o 
ensure that notifications are laid in time.   The C ommittee 
is happy that the Ministry has evolved an internal 
mechanism/ procedure for this purpose.  The Committ ee 
hopes that it would take action accordingly in orde r to 
comply with the prescribed schedule in the matter o f 
laying of statutory Notifications. 
 
The Ministry must take appropriate step to 
remove lacuna, if any, administrative or otherwise,  
causing such long delay by being little proactive a nd 
prompt.  Further, the Ministries should take it up with the 
Ministry of Urban Development for late receiving of  
printed copies of the Notification.”

 The Committee approve the following draft revised 
formula for laying of Statutory Rules before both H ouses 
of Parliament which the Ministry of Law and Justice  
propose to incorporate in all future legislation wh ich 
provide for making of rules by the CentralGovernment:— 
 
 "Every rule made by the Central Government under 
this Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is 
made, before each House of Parliament, while it is in 
session, for a total period of thirty days which ma y be 
comprised in one session or in two or more successi ve 

sessions, and if, before the expiry of the session 
immediately following the session or the successive  
sessions aforesaid, both Houses agree in making any  
modification in the rule or both Houses agree that the 
rule should not be made, the rule shall thereafter 
have effect only in such modified form or be of no 
effect, as the case may be; so, however that any su ch 
modification or annulment shall be without prejudic e 
to the validity of anything previously done under t hat 
rule." 
  
 The Committee recommend that the revised 
formula should be incorporated not only in new 
legislation but also in the existing Acts as and wh en Bills 
to amend them are brought before Parliament. The 
Ministry should also incorporate the new formula in  the 
Bills pending before Parliament. This will, in the opinion 
of the Committee, bring about uniformity in the mat ter 
expeditiously.

Ministries/Departments are neither able to complete  the 
task of framing rules/regulations under different A cts 
within the given six months’ period nor do they suo-motu  
approach the Committee for seeking extension of tim e. 
The Committee further notes that in order to ensure  
timely framing of rules/regulations it has taken an  
initiative to monitor the progress of framing of 
subordinate legislation in respect of all legislati ons 
brought about by different Ministries/Departments o f 
Government of India from the year 2003 onwards with  a 
view to ensure that the framing of subordinate legi slation 
is not delayed. The Committee, however, finds that the 
responses from the Ministries/Departments have not been 
prompt in this monitoring exercise undertaken on be half 
of the Committee. 
  
 In view of the above position, the Committee once 
again reiterates its recommendation that the 
Ministries/Departments should ensure putting in pla ce 
subordinate legislation positively within a period of six 
months of coming into force of the Act. The Committ ee 
further recommends that in case the Ministry fails to meet 
with this deadline, they should invariably approach  the 
Committee for seeking extension of time. The Commit tee 
further recommends that in cases where the time lim it of 
six months is not adhered to, they should, while la ying 
rules/regulations before the Parliament invariably lay a 
statement explaining the reasons why the framing of  
rules/regulations was delayed beyond six months so as to 
keep the Parliament apprised of the compliance of t he 
Parliament’s mandate  conferred upon the Executive.” 

(192 
nd 
 Report) 
(Presented on 26 th   August 2011)  
 
  Rules/Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are laid by 
different Ministries on the Table of the House unde r 
various provisions of parent Acts passed by Parliam ent. 
These Rules/ Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are publis hed 
in the official Gazette before being laid on the Table of the 
House. Even after they are laid, it is very difficu lt to get 
access to these Notifications. The Committee recomm ends 
that such Rules/Regulations/Orders, etc. laid on th e Table 
of the House should be invariably uploaded on the 
websites of respective Ministries immediately on th e same 
day when they have been laid on the Table of the Ho use, 
for information of Members of Parliament and people  at 
large for their easy access. 
201 
st  Report 
(Presented on 14 th  December, 2012)  
 
The Committee observes that the whole process of 
enacting laws is defeated if rules are not framed a nd laid 
on the Table of the House in time.  A reasonable de lay 
could be understood but unjustifiably long delays s hould 
be avoided and the Ministries should work towards 
improving this position.   The Committee hopes that 
Ministry would strive to keep the delay to the mini mum 
and take care that Notifications are laid on the Ta ble of 
the House at the first available opportunity after 
publication of Notifications. 
 
The Committee would like to impress upon the 
Ministry that it is their responsibility to ensure that copies 
of the Notifications are printed timely and for thi s 

purpose, they need to evolve a suitable mechanism t o 
ensure that notifications are laid in time.   The C ommittee 
is happy that the Ministry has evolved an internal 
mechanism/ procedure for this purpose.  The Committ ee 
hopes that it would take action accordingly in orde r to 
comply with the prescribed schedule in the matter o f 
laying of statutory Notifications. 
 
The Ministry must take appropriate step to 
remove lacuna, if any, administrative or otherwise,  
causing such long delay by being little proactive a nd 
prompt.  Further, the Ministries should take it up with the 
Ministry of Urban Development for late receiving of  
printed copies of the Notification. 
212 
th   Report 
(Presented on  3 rd  September, 2013) 
 
 “The Committee is not inclined to accept the late 
availability of printed copies of Notifications fro m the 
Government of India Press as the reason for delay i n 
laying of the Notifications. The Committee directs all the 
Ministries that in case there is a delay in procuri ng 
printed copies in time, they may obtain G.S.R. and S.O. 
numbers from the Government of India Press and 
prepare requisite number of copies in cyclostyled form for 
laying in the Parliament. The Committee also 
recommends that this process may be adopted by 
Ministries suo moto  on immediate basis so as to avoid such 
delays henceforth”.

wise, in a  Statement placed at Annexure . Out of the total

2.  While scrutinizing these Orders, the Committee note d 
that in some cases there was a considerable time la g between 
issue  of Notifications and their laying on the Tab le of the 
Council. The annexed statement also indicates the p eriod of 
delay in cases where Notifications have not been la id as per 
the time schedule recommended by the Committee. The  
Committee observed that out of the total 65 delayed  
Notifications, there were 59 Notifications where no  delay 
statement was appended to and merely 6 Notification s had 
delay statement attached. Further, the bulk of dela yed 
Notifications were from the Ministry of  Finance (Department 
of Revenue), which comes to around 42% of the total  delayed 
Notifications. 
 

The observations/recommendations of the Committee 
in respect of the specific Ministries/Departments w here delay 
in laying of Notifications has been noticed, are as follows: -  
 
(i) Ministry of Finance 
(a)  (Department of Economic Affairs) 
  
The Ministry of Finance (Department of Economic 
Affairs) have laid 25 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 66 to  90), out of 
which 8 Notifications have been delayed.  Out of 8 delayed 
Notifications,  4 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 66 
–  68 & 75) have  
been delayed by 7 months to 8  months and have no d elay 
statements attached to them. Another 4 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 
71 – 74) delayed with huge delay period from 4 years and  1 
month to 9 years  and 9 months, though all of them have been 
accompanied with delay statements. The reasons forw arded 
by the Ministry for delay is as under:- 
  
  “Pursuant to the publication of the Gazette 
Notifications i.e. Securities and Exchange Board of  
India (issue and Listing of Debt Securities) 
Regulations, 2008 and Securities and Exchange Board  
of India (Public Offer and Listing of Securitised D ebt 
Instruments) Regulations, 2008 in the Gazette of In dia 
on 26.05.2008 and 06.06.2008 the concerned Branch 
was required to lay the same in both Houses of 
Parliament. Now, Securities and Exchange Board of 
India (SEBI) has informed that these Gazette 
Notifications have not been laid in Rajya Sabha whi le 
these have been laid in the Lok Sabha. Inadvertentl y 
these were not laid possibly due to unavailability of 
dates in the relevant session or some other reason. 

  Therefore, as a matter of abundant caution, we 
may get the same laid in Rajya Sabha in the upcomin g 
session of Parliament. The same is highly regretted.” 
 
 2. “Pursuant to the publication of the SEBI 
(Intermediaries) Regulations, 2008 in Gazette of In dia 
on 26.05.2008 and SEBI (Investment Advisers) 
Regulations, 2013 in Gazette of India on 21.01.2013 , 
the concerned Department was required to lay down 
the same in both the Houses of Parliament. 
Inadvertently, However, it is observed that the SEB I 
(Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013 have not 
been laid in either House while the SEBI 
(Intermediaries) Regulations, 2008 have been laid i n 
the Lok Sabha but not in the Rajya Sabha. 
  Therefore, as  matter of abundant caution, we 
may get the same laid in Rajya  Sabha in the 
upcoming session of Parliament. The delay in the 
same is highly regretted.” 
 
 The Committee find the reply given by the 
Ministry of Finance (Department of Economic Affairs )  
that the Notifications could not be laid on time du e to 
inadvertence as unacceptable more so when three of them 
were laid in Lok Sabha but not in Rajya Sabha. 
Concerned organization may be  oblivious of this 
requirement but how the Ministry can be found wanti ng 
on this count that Notification is laid on the Tabl e of one 
House and not the other. It only reflects the lack of 
seriousness on the part of the Ministry in fulfilli ng its 
constitutional responsibility to Parliament. The 
Committee expects the Ministry to be more careful a bout 
laying of its papers and see that concerned 

Department/concerned Branch responsible for this ar e 
held accountable so that there are no such recurrences. 
 
 The Committee hopes that the 
Ministry/Department would avoid such instances of 
undue delay in laying of subordinate legislation in  future 
and would remove lacuna, administrative or otherwis e, 
causing delay. The Committee also advises the Minis try to 
avoid recurrence of delays due to administrative reasons. 
 
(b)   (Department of Financial Services) 
 
 The Ministry of Finance (Department of Financial 
Services) have laid 74 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 91 t o 164).  Out 
of these, 7 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 91 
– 93, 138 – 139, 155  & 
156) have been  delayed by a period ranging from  6  months 
to 11 months. Moreover, there is no delay statement  
appended to any of these delayed Notifications.  
 
 The Committee is unhappy with the delay in laying 
of Notifications by the Ministry of Finance (Depart ment 
of Financial Services) and also by the fact that th e 
Ministry didn’t fulfill its duty of attaching delay  
statements as required. The Committee, therefore, d irects 
that the Ministry of Finance (Department of Financi al 
Services) may append delay statements whenever ther e is 
delay in laying of Notifications and avoid recurren ce of 
such delays in future.  
 
 (c) (Department of Revenue) 
 
 The  Ministry of Finance (Department of Revenue) 
have laid 174 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 165 to 338) o n the Table 
of the House. Out of these, 27 Notifications (Sl. N os. 165 
– 

176, 202 – 214 & 216 – 217) have been delayed by 6 to 10 
months and no delay statement has been attached to any of 
these delayed Notifications. 
 
 The Committee appreciates the hard work put in 
by the Ministry of Finance (Department of Revenue) in 
laying of fairly large number of Notifications on t he Table 
of the House in time and keeping the delay in layin g the 
Notifications to the minimum.  However, the Committ ee 
takes strong exception to the Ministry’s failure to  attach  
the delay statements thereto. The Committee, in the  
absence of delay statements, are not able to know t he 
reasons behind these delays. Therefore, the Committ ee 
invites attention to its recommendation contained i n its 
135 
th  Report  in this connection wherein it has been 
emphasized to append invariably a delay statement i n 
case of delay in laying of notifications by  the Mi nistry. 
The Ministry of Finance (Department of Revenue) sho uld 
also endeavour to avoid recurrence of such delays i n 
future. 
 
(ii) Ministry of  Civil Aviation  
  
 The Ministry of Civil Aviation  have laid 6 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 8 to 13)  during the Sessio n and all of 
them have been delayed. The delay period ranges fro m 5 to 
14 months. Moreover, the  Ministry did not append a  delay 
statement citing the reasons for such delay on thei r part as is 
required from them. 
 
 The Committee is not happy to note that all the si x 
Notifications that Ministry of Civil Aviation have laid, 
have been delayed by five months to fourteenth mont hs 
and  no reason has been given for this delay.  This  is in 

contravention of Committee’s recommendation that 
Notification which are delayed, should invariably b e 
accompanied by a delay statement given in its 135 
th   
Report. The Committee would like the Ministry of Ci vil 
Aviation to take necessary steps to obviate such de lays, 
and in case of one delay in laying of Notifications , a delay 
statement should invariably be furnished and laid o n the 
Table of the Council.  
 
(iii) Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs 
 
The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs have laid  
5 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 384 to 388), out of these  only one 
Notification (Sl.No. 386) has been delayed and that  too by 1 
year. There was no delay statement appended thereto. 
 
 The Committee expresses its deep concern over the 
inordinate delay that has taken place in the laying  of only 
one Notification. The Committee  also takes serious  note 
of the fact that the Ministry has not appended any delay 
statement with the delayed Notification. The Committee is 
wondering how cause of this inordinate delay can be  
ascertained in absence of any delay statement. The 
Committee, therefore,  recommends that the Ministry  of 
Housing and Urban Affairs should take all necessary  
precautions in future to avoid recurrence of such 
situations and append delay statements invariably.  
 
(iv) Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate 
Change 
 
The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate 
Change  have laid 3 Notifications (Sl. No. 63 to 65 ). One of 

the Notification (Sl. No. 63) has  been delayed by 10 months 
and no delay statement was appended to it. 
 
 The Committee is constrained to note  that 1 out o f 
3 Notifications laid by the Ministry of Environment , 
Forest and Climate Change, on the Table of the Coun cil 
during the Session, was delayed and no reasons were  
given for the same. As a result, Committee is not a ware of 
the reason for this delay. The Committee view this very 
seriously and feels that not appending the delay 
statements is akin to infringement of Parliament’s right to 
know the facts of the case. Hence, the Committee 
reiterates  its recommendations, as contained in it s 131 
st  
and 135 th  Reports, emphasizing timely laying of  
Notifications  on the Table of the Council and appending a 
delay statement wherever there has been a delay. 
 
(v) Ministry of Human Resource Development 
 (Department of Higher Education) 
  
The Ministry of Human Resource Development 
(Department of Higher Education) have laid 7 Notifi cations 
(Sl. Nos. 389 to 395) during the Session. Out of th ese, one 
Notification (Sl. No. 393) has been delayed by 9 mo nths and 
has no delay statement appended to it. 
 
 The Committee is unhappy over the delay in laying 
of one of its Notification on the Table of the Coun cil. The 
Committee desires the Ministry of Human Resource 
Development (Department of Higher Education) to 
strictly adhere to the time schedule in laying of 
Notifications. The Committee further stresses that the 
Ministry of Human Resource Development (Department 
of Higher Education) should append a delay statemen t 

where there is delay in laying of Notification on t he Table 
of the Council. 
 
(vi) Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas 
 
 The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas have lai d 
3 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 418 to 420), out of which , one 
Notification  (Sl. No. 418) has been delayed by 8 m onths and 
no delay statement has been appended with the Notification. 
   
 The Committee finds that the Ministry of 
Petroleum and Natural Gas have not only delayed the  
laying of Notifications but have also failed to app end 
delay statements thereto. The Committee, in the abs ence 
of delay statements, are not able to know the actua l 
reasons behind the delay in laying of Notifications . The 
Committee have clearly mentioned in its 135 
th  Report that 
delay statements should invariably be appended to t he 
Notification whenever there is a delay in laying of  
Notifications. The Committee, therefore, impresses upon 
the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas to strict ly 
adhere to the time schedule as prescribed in Commit tee’s 
Report, and in case of any delay in a laying, a del ay 
statement should invariably be appended thereto. 
 
 
(vii)  Ministry of Health and Family Welfare 
  (Department of Health and Family Welfare) 
 
 The Ministry of  Health and Family Welfare 
(Department of Health and Family Welfare)  have laid  9 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 343 to 351). Out of these, 3 
Notifications  (Sl. Nos. 343 
– 345) have been delayed. The 
delay period ranges from 7 months to 8 months and t he 

Ministry have failed to append delay statement to any of these 
delayed Notifications. 
 
 The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry 
of Health and Family Welfare (Department of Health and 
Family Welfare)   have made delays in laying of 
Notifications and no delay statement has been appen ded 
to any of them. As a result of the absence of delay  
statements, the Committee is not able to know the r easons 
of such delays. The Committee would like the Minist ry to 
take corrective measures to curtail such delays in future, 
and in case such delay does take place, it should 
invariably be accompanied by statements giving the 
reasons for the delay in laying. 
 
(viii) Ministry of Home Affairs 
  
The Ministry of Home Affairs have laid 32 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 352 to 383), out of which, 4 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 357 
– 358 & 369 – 370) were delayed 
by 7  months in each cases. Not even a single Notification has 
been appended with a delay statement, whatsoever, 
explaining reasons therefor. 
 
 The Committee, further reiterates that in the 
absence of delay statements, they are not able to k now the 
reasons behind the delay in laying of these Notific ations. 
The Committee have clearly mentioned in its 135 
th  Report 
that delay statements should invariably be appended  
where there is delay in laying of Notifications. Th e 
Committee, therefore, impress upon the Ministry of Home 
Affairs to strictly adhere to the time schedule as 
prescribed in Committee’s Report that in case of an y 
delay in laying, delay statement should invariably be 

appended so that the valid reasons for such delay a re 
brought to its notice. 
 
(ix) Ministry of Electronics and Information 
Technology 
 
 The Ministry of Electronics and Information 
Technology have laid 5 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 58 t o 62),  out 
of which 4 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 58 
– 61) have been delayed 
by five months to twelve months and there is no del ay 
statement attached to any of these delayed Notifications.  
 
 The Committee is not happy over the delay of 5 
months, 8 months and 1 year in laying of  4 Notific ations   
by the Ministry of Electronics and Information 
Technology. Further, there is no delay statement 
appended thereto giving details as to what caused s uch a 
long delay. The Committee, therefore, impresses upo n the 
Ministry to take care that such instances of delay do not 
recur in future and in case of any delay in laying,  a delay 
statement detailing the reasons for such delay shou ld 
invariably be appended thereto. 
 
(x) Ministry of Corporate Affairs 
  
 The Ministry of Corporate Affairs have laid 23 
Notifications ( Sl. Nos. 34 to 56), out of which, 2  
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 34 & 43) have been delayed.  The 
delay period ranges  from 5 to 9 months and both of  delayed 
Notifications have appended with delay statements. The 
reasons for delay  given by the Ministry is  as under:- 
  
 “In terms of the requirement of Section 18 (5B) of  the 
Chartered Accountants Act, 1949 a copy of the annua l 

report and audited accounts of the Institute are 
required to be published in the Gazette of India no t 
later than 30 
th  day of September of the year next 
following.  Further in terms of Section 30B of the said 
Act copies of the said Gazette of India are require d to 
be laid before both Houses of the Parliament. 
Accordingly, the notification dated 28 
th  September, 
2017 containing the Annual Report of audited 
accounts of the Institute for the year ended 31 
st  March, 
2017 was published in the gazette of India, 
extraordinary dated 29 
th  September, 2017. However, 
some compilation errors, accounting mistakes, 
discrepancies in disclosure and major mismatching 
with previous year figures in the audited financial s 
were noticed in the 68 
th  Annual Report and Audited 
Accounts. Accordingly, a corrigendum dated 21 st  
December, 2017 rectifying the errors contained in t he 
above mentioned notification has been published in 
the Gazette of India, Extraordinary dated 21 
st  
December, 2017. 
 
 In view of the aforesaid reasons, the 68 
th  Annual 
Reports and Audited  Accounts could not be laid on the 
Tables of both the Houses of the  Parliament. Hence , the 
Delay Statement.” 
 
 “The Notification relating to the G.S.R. No. 880(E ), 
dated 23.07.2017  on Companies (Meetings of Board a nd 
its Powers) Second Amendment  Rules, 2017 was 
required to be laid before both the Houses of 
 Parliament during the Monsoon Session, 2017. 
 
 The above Notification G.S.R. No. 880(E), dated 
23.07.2017 on Companies (Meetings of Board and its 

Powers) Second Amendment Rules, 2017 was sent to 
Government Press for printing. The said notificatio n 
could not be laid before both the Houses of Parliament 
during the Monsoon Session of the Parliament, 2017 
as e-Gazette copy of the said notification was not 
uploaded by the Directorate of Printing, D/o 
Publication and when it was uploaded both Sessions 
of Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha were over. The said 
notification got delayed and hence it may be kindly  be 
condoned.” 
 
The Committee does not accept the reason for 
delay i.e., the compilation errors, accounting mist akes,  
and that the e-Gazette copy of the said notificatio n was 
not uploaded by the Department of Printing, D/o 
Publication, as given by the Ministry of Corporate 
Affairs. The Committee does not accept these as 
convincing reasons in respect of laying of statutory papers 
before the Parliament. 
 
 The Committee, time and again, have emphasized 
that laying of rules/regulations/orders is a statut ory 
obligation of the Ministries and should be complete d on 
priority within specified time-frame. The Ministry of 
Corporate Affairs should understand the implication s of 
such failures. The Ministry has, by these delays, n ot only 
violated the recommendations of the Committee but a lso 
violated the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949 by del aying 
the publication of the Notification in the official  Gazette 
before 30 
th  September, 2017. 
  
 The Committee, therefore,  reiterates its earlier 
direction contained in its 131 
st  Report to all the Ministries 
that if the Council  is not in Session, the order s hould be 

laid during the Session immediately following the d ate of 
publication of the order in the Official Gazette an d if the 
Council is in Session and the date of Gazette Notif ication 
is within 15 days of following closure of the Sessi on, then 
it should be laid before the expiry of the Session 
immediately following. In case there is delay in pr ocuring 
printed copies in time, they may as recommended by the 
Committee in its 212 
th  Report, obtain G.S.R. and S.O. 
numbers from the Government of India Press and 
prepare requisite number of copies in cyclostyled form for 
laying in the Parliament as suggested by Secretary,  
Ministry of  Urban Development, the controlling Min istry 
of Government of India Press, in its meeting held o n 30 
th  
July, 2013. The Committee also once again recommend s 
that this process may be adopted by Ministries suo moto  
on immediate basis so as to avoid such delays henceforth. 
 
3.   The Committee impresses upon all the 
Ministries/Departments to take immediate and concre te steps 
to ensure timely and proper laying of subordinate l egislation. 
The Committee, accordingly, wishes to bring to the notice of 
all Ministries/Departments of the Government of Ind ia, 
particularly, the defaulting ones, the following 
recommendations, as contained in its 7 
th , 10 th , 131 
st 
, 135 
th 
, 
152 
nd ,  192 nd  , 201 st , 212 th  and 213 th  Reports: 
 
 “The Committee desires that for the convenience 
of the public and Members, Ministries should hencef orth 
send copies of 'order' duly authenticated by the Mi nisters 
concerned, incorporating therein all the correction s and 
amendments issued till date of laying such 'orders' instead 
of laying the uncorrected copy along with corrigend a. The 
Committee feels that to obviate any legal or techni cal 

difficulty, Ministries should examine whether there  is any 
necessity of assigning a separate G.S.R. No. to a 
corrigendum at the time of its publication in the G azette 
and whether such a corrigendum should not be publis hed 
without assigning any G.S.R. No. The Committee woul d, 
therefore, like to impress upon all Ministries of t he 
Government of India that the present practice of la ying 
the rules without incorporating corrigenda in the b ody of 
the rules is not a healthy one. The Committee hopes  that 
the Ministries will ensure supply of only corrected  copies 
of the rules for laying on the Table so that they d epict a 
true and correct picture and serve the desired purp ose." 
  
(7 
th   Report) 
(Presented on 12 th   May, 1969) 
 
 
 The Committee approve the following draft revised 
formula for laying of Statutory Rules before both H ouses 
of Parliament which the Ministry of Law and Justice  
propose to incorporate in all future legislation wh ich 
provide for making of rules by the CentralGovernment:— 
 
 "Every rule made by the Central Government under 
this Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is 
made, before each House of Parliament, while it is in 
session, for a total period of thirty days which ma y be 
comprised in one session or in two or more successi ve 
sessions, and if, before the expiry of the session 
immediately following the session or the successive  
sessions aforesaid, both Houses agree in making any  
modification in the rule or both Houses agree that the 
rule should not be made, the rule shall thereafter 
have effect only in such modified form or be of no 

effect, as the case may be; so, however that any su ch 
modification or annulment shall be without prejudic e 
to the validity of anything previously done under t hat 
rule." 
  
The Committee recommend that the revised formula 
should be incorporated not only in new legislation but also 
in the existing Acts as and when Bills to amend the m are 
brought before Parliament. The Ministry should also  
incorporate the new formula in the Bills pending be fore 
Parliament. This will, in the opinion of the Commit tee, 
bring about uniformity in the matter expeditiously. 
 
(10 
th   Report) 
(presented on 24 th  May, 1971) 
 
 
 “Orders required to be laid before the House shoul d 
be laid (i) if the House is not in Session, during the Session 
immediately following the date of publication of the Order 
in the Official Gazette and (ii) if the House is in  Session, 
on the date of the publication of the Order, during  its 
continuance and in case the time lag between the da te of 
publication and the date of the closing of the Sess ion is 
less than 15 clear days, before the expiry of the S ession 
immediately following the said Session. All the 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India shoul d 
henceforth comply with this schedule in the matter of 
laying of the Orders issued under various Acts of 
Parliament on the Table of the Rajya Sabha. 
 
(131 st  Report) 
(Presented on 15 
th   December 2000) 

 
 
 
 “The Committee has, time and again, emphasized 
that it is essential that in case there is a delay in the laying 
of Statutory Orders, the concerned Ministry/Departm ent 
should invariably append a delay statement along with the 
Notifications being laid so as to apprise Parliamen t of the 
causes of delay. The Committee desires all 
Ministries/Departments to take a note of this, sinc e the 
intention is that through the process of formulatio n of a 
delay statement, the Ministry is able to introspect, identify 
bottlenecks and devise remedial measures”. 
(135 th  Report) 
(Presented on 27 
th   July 2001) 
 
 “In the opinion of the Committee, every notificati on 
should be assigned a distinctive number in order to  give it 
a separate identity and similarly, no notification should be 
published/laid which does not carry a notification 
number. The Committee expects all 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India to 
exercise caution in this regard. In case where ther e are 
more than one Notifications under a single file, th e 
Ministries/Departments should ensure that the file 
number on each notification should be suitably 
distinguished from one another.” 
(152 
nd 
 Report) 
(Presented on 26 th   August 2004)  
 
 “In addition to the concern expressed by the 
Committee over delay in laying of Notifications on the 

Table of the House, the Committee also express thei r deep 
concern over delay in framing of rules/regulations under 
different Acts. The Committee in its 47 th  report presented 
to the House on 14.9.1981 has recommended that the rule-
making process should be completed within a period of six 
months of the coming into force of an Act. The Committee 
has further recommended that in case a Ministry is not 
able to adhere to this time limit, it should seek e xtension 
of time for completing the rule-making process. The  
recommendation of the committee reads as follows:- 
 
  “The Committee feels that the rule-
making process could well have been completed 
within the time limit of six months which the 
Committee has laid down for making of rules 
under an Act after coming into force of that Act. 
Where however, a Ministry does not find it possible 
to adhere to the time limit, they should inform the  
Committee of the reasons why they cannot make 
rules within the time limit and seek extension of 
time for completing the rule-making process.” 
  
 The Committee is constrained to take note of the 
fact that the Ministries/Departments of Government of 
India are not complying with the Committee’s 
recommendation to complete the process of framing o f 
subordinate legislation contemplated under various Acts 
of Parliament within a period of six months. At the  same 
time, the Committee also does not receive requests for 
extension of time for completing the rule-making pr ocess 
in terms of its recommendations as above from most of 
the Ministries/Departments. The Committee takes a 
serious note of the prevailing situation in which t he 

Ministries/Departments are neither able to complete  the 
task of framing rules/regulations under different A cts 
within the given six months’ period nor do they suo-motu  
approach the Committee for seeking extension of tim e. 
The Committee further notes that in order to ensure  
timely framing of rules/regulations it has taken an  
initiative to monitor the progress of framing of 
subordinate legislation in respect of all legislati ons 
brought about by different Ministries/Departments o f 
Government of India from the year 2003 onwards with  a 
view to ensure that the framing of subordinate legi slation 
is not delayed. The Committee, however, finds that the 
responses from the Ministries/Departments have not been 
prompt in this monitoring exercise undertaken on be half 
of the Committee. 
  
 In view of the above position, the Committee once 
again reiterates its recommendation that the 
Ministries/Departments should ensure putting in pla ce 
subordinate legislation positively within a period of six 
months of coming into force of the Act. The Committ ee 
further recommends that in case the Ministry fails to meet 
with this deadline, they should invariably approach  the 
Committee for seeking extension of time. The Commit tee 
further recommends that in cases where the time lim it of 
six months is not adhered to, they should, while la ying 
rules/regulations before the Parliament invariably lay a 
statement explaining the reasons why the framing of  
rules/regulations was delayed beyond six months so as to 
keep the Parliament apprised of the compliance of t he 
Parliament’s mandate  conferred upon the Executive.” 
(192 
nd 
 Report) 
(Presented on 26 th   August 2011)  

 
  Rules/Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are laid by 
different Ministries on the Table of the House unde r 
various provisions of parent Acts passed by Parliam ent. 
These Rules/ Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are publis hed 
in the official Gazette before being laid on the Table of the 
House. Even after they are laid, it is very difficu lt to get 
access to these Notifications. The Committee recomm ends 
that such Rules/Regulations/Orders, etc. laid on th e Table 
of the House should be invariably uploaded on the 
websites of respective Ministries immediately on th e same 
day when they have been laid on the Table of the Ho use, 
for information of Members of Parliament and people  at 
large for their easy access. 
201 
st  Report 
(Presented on 14 th  December, 2012)  
 
The Committee observes that the whole process of 
enacting laws is defeated if rules are not framed a nd laid 
on the Table of the House in time.  A reasonable de lay 
could be understood but unjustifiably long delays s hould 
be avoided and the Ministries should work towards 
improving this position.   The Committee hopes that 
Ministry would strive to keep the delay to the mini mum 
and take care that Notifications are laid on the Ta ble of 
the House at the first available opportunity after 
publication of Notifications. 
 
The Committee would like to impress upon the 
Ministry that it is their responsibility to ensure that copies 
of the Notifications are printed timely and for thi s 
purpose, they need to evolve a suitable mechanism t o 
ensure that notifications are laid in time.   The C ommittee 
is happy that the Ministry has evolved an internal 

mechanism/ procedure for this purpose.  The Committ ee 
hopes that it would take action accordingly in orde r to 
comply with the prescribed schedule in the matter o f 
laying of statutory Notifications. 
 
The Ministry must take appropriate step to 
remove lacuna, if any, administrative or otherwise,  
causing such long delay by being little proactive a nd 
prompt.  Further, the Ministries should take it up with the 
Ministry of Urban Development for late receiving of  
printed copies of the Notification. 
212 
th   Report 
(Presented on  3 rd  September, 2013) 
 
 “The Committee is not inclined to accept the late 
availability of printed copies of Notifications fro m the 
Government of India Press as the reason for delay i n 
laying of the Notifications. The Committee directs all the 
Ministries that in case there is a delay in procuri ng 
printed copies in time, they may obtain G.S.R. and S.O. 
numbers from the Government of India Press and 
prepare requisite number of copies in cyclostyled form for 
laying in the Parliament. The Committee also 
recommends that this process may be adopted by 
Ministries suo moto  on immediate basis so as to avoid such 
delays henceforth”.

2.  While scrutinizing these Orders, the Committee note d 
that there was a considerable time lag between issu e  of 
Notifications and their laying in some cases. The a nnexed 
statement also indicates the period of delay in cas es where 
Notifications have not been laid as per the time sc hedule 
prescribed by the Committee. The Committee observed  that 
out of the total 67 delayed Notifications, there we re 52 
Notifications where no delay statement was appended  to. The 
bulk of delayed Notifications were from the Ministr y of  
Road Transport and Highways which comes to around 4 6.2% 
of the total delayed Notifications. 
 

The observations/recommendations of the Committee 
in respect of the specific Ministries/Departments w here delay 
in laying of Notifications has been noticed, are as follows: -  
 
(i) Ministry of Health & Family Welfare 
 (Department of Health & Family Welfare) 
 
 The Ministry of Health & Family Welfare 
(Department of Health & Family Welfare)   have laid 17 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 316 to 332) on the Table of  the 
Council during the Session, and  11 Notification ha ve been 
delayed.  7 Notification (Sl. Nos. 324 – 330) have been laid 
with huge delay period ranging from 5 years 8 month s to 36 
years and 8 months though all of them have been 
accompanied with delay statements. Whereas 4 other  
Notifications have been delayed by 4 months to 10 m onths 
and there is no delay statement attached thereto. T he reasons 
cited by the Ministry for delay are  as under:- 
 
 “As per the provision 29(3) of the All India Insti tute 
of Medical Sciences, Act, 1956 every regulation mad e under 
this section shall be laid, as soon as may be after  it is made, 
before each House of Parliament, while it is in ses sion, for a 
total period of thirty days, which may be comprised  in one 
session or in two or more successive sessions, and if, before 
the expiry of the sessions immediately following th e sessions 
or the successive sessions aforesaid, both Houses a gree in 
making any modifications in the regulation or both Houses 
agree that the regulation should not be made, the r egulation 
shall thereafter have effect only in such modified form or be 
of no effect, as the case may be, so however that a ny such 
modification or annulment shall be without prejudic e to the 
validity of anything previously done under that regulation. 

 Delay in laying the Regulation in both the Houses of 
Parliament has occurred due to oversight in the Ins titute. The 
said delay is sincerely regretted.”  
 
 This Committee regrets to say that there is delay in 
laying of almost 64.7% of Notifications that the Mi nistry 
of Health & Family Welfare (Department of Health & 
Family Welfare) have laid. Further 4 Notifications have a 
long and undue delay ranging from fifteen years two  
months to thirty-six years and ten months,  3 Notif ications 
have a delay period ranging from five years and eig hth 
months to eight years and eighth months and 4 
Notifications have a delay period of five months to  ten 
months! The Committee cannot simply accept the reas on 
given by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare  
(Department of Health)  that the Notifications could not be 
laid on time due to oversight. This is not comprehe nsible 
as how this inordinate delay can happen due to over sight. 
The delay period is very high. Furthermore, there i s no 
delay statement appended to any of these delayed 
Notifications which is again unacceptable. No delay  
statement coupled with inordinate delay is quite enigmatic 
to the Committee. The Committee always makes a poin t 
that Ministry should have appended a delay statemen t so 
as to apprise the Parliament of the reasons of dela y in 
laying of Notifications on the Table of the Houses.  The  
Ministry of Health & Family Welfare (Department of 
Health & Family Welfare) should inquire the excessi ve 
delay period in laying of the Notifications and tak e 
corrective steps. The Committee reiterates its 
recommendations as contained in its 131 
st  and 135 th  
Reports emphasizing timely laying of  Notifications   on 
the Table of the Council and appending a delay stat ement 
wherever there has been a delay. Not appending a de lay 

statement is akin to infringement of Parliament’s r ight to 
know the facts of the case. The Committee takes a s erious 
note of the matter and urges the Ministry to be car eful in 
future.   
 
(ii)  Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate 
Change 
  
 Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change  
have laid 12 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 85 to 96) duri ng the 
Session. Out of these 5 Notifications, (Sl. Nos. 86  - 90) have 
been delayed by 6 months to 1 year and 5 months and  no 
delay statement is attached to any of the delayed 
Notifications.  
   
 The Committee are pained to notice that out of 12 
Notifications which Ministry of Environment, Forest  and 
Climate Change have laid, five Notifications have b een 
delayed from 6 months to 17 months. Further, there is no 
reason given for this inordinate delay.  This is in  
contravention to Committee’s recommendation given i n 
its 135 
th  Report that Notifications which are delayed 
should invariably be accompanied by delay statement s. 
The Committee would like the Ministry of Environmen t, 
Forest and Climate Change to take necessary steps t o 
obviate such delays and in case of delay in laying of 
Notifications, a delay statement should invariably be 
appended with them.  
 
(iii) Ministry of  Home Affairs 
 
Ministry of Home Affairs  have laid 15 Notification s 
(Sl. No. 333 to 347). Two of them (Sl. No. 333 and 334) have 
been delayed by 11 months and 9 months respectively and are 

accompanied with delay statement. The reason given by the 
Ministry for delay is as under:-. 
 
 “The Notification No. 266/2017/F.No. 27-4/2014-
Rev. dated 06.11.2017 (English version) in respect of 
‘the Andaman and Nicobar Islands Anand Marriage 
Registration Rule, 2017’ and Notification No. 
ADM/LAW/29/2017/1747 DATED 04.09.2017 
(English version) in respect of  ‘the Dadra and Nag ar 
Haveli Anand Marriages Registration Rules, 2017’ 
were published by UT Administrations of Andaman & 
Nicobar Islands and Dadra and Nagar Haveli 
respectively under section 6 of the Anand Marriage 
Act, 1909 (7 of 1909) as amended by the Anand 
Marriage (Amendment) Act, 2012 (29 of 2012). The 
notification could not be laid on the table of the 
Houses due to the delay in the publication of the Hindi 
version of the Notification by the UT Administration. 
 
 The Hindi version of Notification No. 266/2017/F.N o. 
27-4/2014-Rev. dated 06.11.2017 & 
ADM/LAW/29/2017/1747 DATED 04.09.2017 have 
now been published in the Gazette of Andaman & 
Nicobar Islands and Dadra & Nagar Haveli and 
received in  this Ministry only on 14.05.2016 and 
22.05.2018 in respect of A&NI and DNH 
respectively. Hence Notification (both in Hindi & 
English version) are being laid on the Table of Lok  
Sabha/Rajya Sabha under Section 6(4) of the Anand 
Marriage Act, 1909 (7 of 1909) as amended by the 
Anand Marriage (Amendment) Act, 2012 (29 of 
2012). The aforesaid Hindi version of notifications got 
delayed and which caused further delay in laying th e 
copies (Hindi and English version) to both the Hous es 

of Parliament and it is requested that the same may  
kindly be condoned.” 
 
 The Committee notes with deep concern the delay 
of eleven  months and nine months in laying of the 
Notifications.  The Committee finds that laying of the 
notifications was delayed due to late receipt of th e Hindi 
version of Notification No. 266/2017/F.No. 27-4/201 4-Rev. 
dated 06.11.2017 & ADM/LAW/29/2017/1747 DATED 
04.09.2017 and have now been published in the Gazet te of 
Andaman & Nicobar Islands and Dadra & Nagar Haveli 
and excessive time has been taken in completing the  
procedural formalities in the Ministry of Home Affairs. In 
this context the Committee observes that it is the 
Ministry’s responsibility to ensure that the Subord inate 
Legislation is laid before the Parliament within th e 
prescribed time schedule and accordingly, it is for  the 
Ministry only to ensure that they receive the same timely 
from the statutory bodies under them and complete a ll 
formalities of laying them before the Council is 
adjourned. The Committee recommends that the Ministry 
of Home Affairs may take necessary remedial measures to 
ensure that papers are laid well in time  on the Ta ble of 
the Council. 
 
(iv) Ministry of Road Transport and Highways 
 
The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways have 
laid 84 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 380 to 463). There has been 
significant number of Notifications which have been  delayed. 
Out of 27 delayed Notifications only 4 Notification s (Sl. Nos. 
380 -383) have been attached with delay statement a nd 23 
Notifications have no delay statement appended ther eto. The 
delay period ranges from 5 to 9 months. The reasons given by 

the Ministry is that it took some time to collect the papers and 
complete the procedural formalities. Therefore, Not ifications 
could not be laid in time on the Table of both the Houses of 
Parliament. 
 
The Committee is constrained to observe that 
delay in laying Notifications in such large number is just 
not acceptable to the Committee. Moreover, 23 out o f 27 
Notifications delayed did not have the delay statem ents 
appended thereto. While there may be a reason for t he 
delay, but there cannot be any reason for not furni shing 
reason for that. The Ministry must understand the 
implications for not doing so regularly more so in such a 
large number of cases. 
 
 The Committee does not accept the reasons of the 
delay given by the  Ministry of Road Transport and 
Highways that it took some time to collect the pape rs and 
complete the procedural formalities. The Committee 
wonders how can it take such a long time to receive  
Notifications and to complete procedural formalitie s. The 
Committee feels that the Ministry did not take adeq uate 
precaution to avoid the delay. The Committee furthe r 
makes a point that Ministry should append a delay 
statement in each such cases so as to apprise the 
Parliament of the reasons of delay in laying of 
Notifications on the Table of the Houses. 
 
 
(v) Ministry of  Electronics and Information 
Technology  
  
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology 
have laid 8 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 77 to 84) . Out  of  these  

one  Notification ( Sl. No. 83) have been delayed b y 7 
months. There is no delay statement appended thereto. 
 
The Committee takes a serious view of not only the 
delay in laying of one of its Notifications on the Table of 
the Council but also failure to append a delay stat ement 
with it. The Ministry of Electronics and Informatio n 
Technology must know about the possible implication s of 
failing to meet this requirement. The Committee 
recommends that the  Ministry of  Electronics and 
Information Technology ensure to append a delay 
statement in all such cases in future . 
 
(vi) Ministry of Finance 
(a)  (Department of Financial Services) 
 
Ministry of Finance (Department of Financial 
Services) have laid 11 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 134 to 144), out 
of which 4 Notifications have been delayed.  Out of 4 delayed 
Notifications,  2  Notifications (Sl. Nos. 141 & 14 2) have  
been delayed each by 5 months and have no delay sta tements 
attached to either of them. 2 Notifications (Sl. No s. 137 & 
138) have been delayed  by 6 months with delay stat ement 
appended to both of them. The reasons forwarded by the 
Ministry for delay is as under:- 
 
 “The Notifications dated 29.6.2017 regarding 
amendment in Canara Bank Employees’ Pension 
Regulations, 1995 and Canara Bank Officers’ Service  
Regulations, 1979 were published in the Gazette of 
India, vide No. 2 & 4 dated January 13 – January, 1 9, 
2018 and January 27 – February 2, 2018. The Bank 
furnished the requisite copies of Gazette Notificat ion 
vide their letter dated 6.2.2018 and 14.2.2018. 

However, as the Notification  numbers and name of 
the Bank was not appearing on the first page of the  
publication, revised copies could be sent vide thei r 
letter dated 12.4.2018 and 3.5.2018. The Bank has 
submitted that the delay is not intentional and 
requested that the same may kindly be condoned. 
 
In view of above, the said Notifications could not be 
laid on the Table  of the both the Houses on earlie r 
occasions. Delay in this regard is  deeply regrette d and 
may please be condoned.” 
 
The Committee takes a serious view not only about 
the delay in laying of ten Notifications  by the Mi nistry of 
Finance (Department of Financial Services) on the T able 
of the Council but also of  its failure to append t he 
required delay statement. The Committee observes th at 
Parliamentary sessions are declared much in advance  and 
had the Ministry of Finance (Department of Financia l 
Services) taken prompt steps for laying of the 
notifications, in coordination with Banks for suppl y of 
Gazette Notifications in right form,  the delay cou ld have 
been well avoided. It reflects management/planning on the 
part of the Ministry. The Committee, therefore, 
recommends that the Ministry should complete the 
procedural formalities at the earliest to avoid suc h kind of 
delays in future and invariably attach the delay st atement 
when there is delay in laying the Notification. 
 
 
(b) (Department of Revenue) 
 
 Ministry of Finance (Department of revenue) have 
laid 170 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 145 to 332) during  the 246 
th   

Session. Out of these 7 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 167   & 214 – 
219) have been  delayed by 5 months to 8 months. There is no 
delay statement appended to any of these.  
 
 The Committee appreciates that the Ministry of 
Finance (Department of Revenue) has to lay a huge 
volume of statutory papers during any Parliamentary  
Session.  While only 7 Notifications have been dela yed, 
none had a delay statement appended thereto.  As a result 
Committee does not know the reason for this delay. The 
Committee reiterates  its recommendations as contai ned 
in its 131 
st  and 135 th  Reports emphasizing timely laying of  
Notifications  on the Table of the House and append ing a 
delay statement wherever  there has been a delay. N ot 
appending delay statement is akin to infringement o f 
Parliament’s right to know the facts of the case.  
  
 
(vii) Ministry of Power 
 
Ministry of Power  have laid 4 Notifications (Sl. N os. 
376 to 379) on the Table of the House during the Session. Out 
of which three Notification (Sl. Nos. 377 - 379) ha ve been 
delayed by 5 to 6 months and there is no delay stat ement 
appended to all of  these delayed Notifications. 
 
 The Committee takes a strong view of the delay 
that has occurred in tabling the Notifications and 
emphasise that the Ministry should avoid such insta nces 
of delay in laying of Subordinate Legislation in fu ture. 
The Committee also impresses upon the Ministry to t ake 
note of the fact that in case there is a delay in t he laying of 
any Statutory Notifications, the same should be 
accompanied by a delay statement while it is being laid. 

The Ministry may take steps to avoid delay in layin g and 
also append the delay statement to the Notification s 
whenever there is  delays in laying. 
 
 
 
 (viii) Ministry of Science and Technology 
 (Department of Science and Technology) 
 
 Only one Notification that the Ministry of Science  and 
Technology (Department of Science and Technology) ( Sl. 
No. 464) have laid was delayed by 5 months and no d elay 
statement has been appended therewith. 
 
 The Committee is unhappy over the delay in laying 
of the only  Notification by the Ministry of Scienc e and 
Technology (Department of Science and Technology)   by  
5 months. Further, there is no delay statement appe nded 
thereto giving reasons as to what caused such undue  
delay. The Committee, therefore, impresses upon the  
Ministry to take care that such instances of delay do not 
recur in future and in case of any delay in their l aying, a 
delay statement should invariably be appended therewith. 
 
(ix) Ministry of Textiles 
  
 Ministry of Textiles have laid 7 Notifications (Sl . Nos. 
471 to 477).  Two of them (Sl. Nos. 475 
– 476) have been  
delayed from  7 months or 5 months and Ministry did  not 
append a delay statement citing the reasons for suc h delay on 
their part.  
 
 The Committee is concerned over the delay in 
laying of Notifications by the Ministry of Textiles  

particularly Notifications at Sl. Nos. 475 and 476 where 
delay period spans over  a period between five and  seven 
months. In the absence of any delay statement, Committee 
would not be able to make out the reasons for the d elay 
and suggest remedial measures for rectifying it. Th e 
Committee, therefore, directs that the Ministry of Textiles  
to append delay statements whenever there is delay in 
laying of Notifications and avoid recurrence of suc h 
delays in future.  
 
3.   The Committee impresses upon all the 
Ministries/Departments to take immediate and concre te steps 
to ensure timely and proper laying of subordinate l egislation. 
The Committee, accordingly, wishes to bring to the notice of 
all Ministries/Departments of the Government of Ind ia, 
particularly, the defaulting ones, the following 
recommendations, as contained in its 7 
th , 10 th , 131 
st 
, 135 
th 
, 
152 
nd ,  192 nd  , 201 st , 212 th  and 213 th  Reports: 
 
 “The Committee desires that for the convenience 
of the public and Members, Ministries should hencef orth 
send copies of 'order' duly authenticated by the Mi nisters 
concerned, incorporating therein all the correction s and 
amendments issued till date of laying such 'orders' instead 
of laying the uncorrected copy along with corrigend a. The 
Committee feels that to obviate any legal or techni cal 
difficulty, Ministries should examine whether there  is any 
necessity of assigning a separate G.S.R. No. to a 
corrigendum at the time of its publication in the G azette 
and whether such a corrigendum should not be publis hed 
without assigning any G.S.R. No. The Committee woul d, 
therefore, like to impress upon all Ministries of t he 
Government of India that the present practice of la ying 

the rules without incorporating corrigenda in the b ody of 
the rules is not a healthy one. The Committee hopes  that 
the Ministries will ensure supply of only corrected  copies 
of the rules for laying on the Table so that they d epict a 
true and correct picture and serve the desired purp ose." 
  
(7 th   Report) 
(Presented on 12 th   May, 1969) 
 
 The Committee approve the following draft revised 
formula for laying of Statutory Rules before both H ouses 
of Parliament which the Ministry of Law and Justice  
propose to incorporate in all future legislation wh ich 
provide for making of rules by the Central 
Government:— 
 
 "Every rule made by the Central Government under 
this Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is 
made, before each House of Parliament, while it is in 
session, for a total period of thirty days which ma y be 
comprised in one session or in two or more successi ve 
sessions, and if, before the expiry of the session 
immediately following the session or the successive  
sessions aforesaid, both Houses agree in making any  
modification in the rule or both Houses agree that the 
rule should not be made, the rule shall thereafter 
have effect only in such modified form or be of no 
effect, as the case may be; so, however that any su ch 
modification or annulment shall be without prejudic e 
to the validity of anything previously done under t hat 
rule." 
  
The Committee recommend that the revised formula 
should be incorporated not only in new legislation but also 

in the existing Acts as and when Bills to amend the m are 
brought before Parliament. The Ministry should also  
incorporate the new formula in the Bills pending be fore 
Parliament. This will, in the opinion of the Commit tee, 
bring about uniformity in the matter expeditiously. 
 
(10 th   Report) 
(presented on 24 th  May, 1971) 
 
 
 “Orders required to be laid before the House shoul d 
be laid (i) if the House is not in Session, during the Session 
immediately following the date of publication of the Order 
in the Official Gazette and (ii) if the House is in  Session, 
on the date of the publication of the Order, during  its 
continuance and in case the time lag between the da te of 
publication and the date of the closing of the Sess ion is 
less than 15 clear days, before the expiry of the S ession 
immediately following the said Session. All the 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India shoul d 
henceforth comply with this schedule in the matter of 
laying of the Orders issued under various Acts of 
Parliament on the Table of the Rajya Sabha. 
 
(131 st  Report) 
(Presented on 15 
th   December 2000) 
 
 
 
 “The Committee has, time and again, emphasized 
that it is essential that in case there is a delay in the laying 
of Statutory Orders, the concerned Ministry/Departm ent 
should invariably append a delay statement along with the 

Notifications being laid so as to apprise Parliamen t of the 
causes of delay. The Committee desires all 
Ministries/Departments to take a note of this, sinc e the 
intention is that through the process of formulatio n of a 
delay statement, the Ministry is able to introspect, identify 
bottlenecks and devise remedial measures”. 
(135 th  Report) 
(Presented on 27 
th   July 2001) 
 
 “In the opinion of the Committee, every notificati on 
should be assigned a distinctive number in order to  give it 
a separate identity and similarly, no notification should be 
published/laid which does not carry a notification 
number. The Committee expects all 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India to 
exercise caution in this regard. In case where ther e are 
more than one Notifications under a single file, th e 
Ministries/Departments should ensure that the file 
number on each notification should be suitably 
distinguished from one another.” 
(152 
nd 
 Report) 
(Presented on 26 th   August 2004)  
 
 “In addition to the concern expressed by the 
Committee over delay in laying of Notifications on the 
Table of the House, the Committee also express thei r deep 
concern over delay in framing of rules/regulations under 
different Acts. The Committee in its 47 
th  report presented 
to the House on 14.9.1981 has recommended that the rule-
making process should be completed within a period of six 
months of the coming into force of an Act. The Committee 
has further recommended that in case a Ministry is not 

able to adhere to this time limit, it should seek e xtension 
of time for completing the rule-making process. The  
recommendation of the committee reads as follows:- 
 
  “The Committee feels that the rule-
making process could well have been completed 
within the time limit of six months which the 
Committee has laid down for making of rules 
under an Act after coming into force of that Act. 
Where however, a Ministry does not find it possible 
to adhere to the time limit, they should inform the  
Committee of the reasons why they cannot make 
rules within the time limit and seek extension of 
time for completing the rule-making process.” 
  
 The Committee is constrained to take note of the 
fact that the Ministries/Departments of Government of 
India are not complying with the Committee’s 
recommendation to complete the process of framing o f 
subordinate legislation contemplated under various Acts 
of Parliament within a period of six months. At the  same 
time, the Committee also does not receive requests for 
extension of time for completing the rule-making pr ocess 
in terms of its recommendations as above from most of 
the Ministries/Departments. The Committee takes a 
serious note of the prevailing situation in which t he 
Ministries/Departments are neither able to complete  the 
task of framing rules/regulations under different A cts 
within the given six months’ period nor do they suo-motu  
approach the Committee for seeking extension of tim e. 
The Committee further notes that in order to ensure  
timely framing of rules/regulations it has taken an  
initiative to monitor the progress of framing of 

subordinate legislation in respect of all legislati ons 
brought about by different Ministries/Departments o f 
Government of India from the year 2003 onwards with  a 
view to ensure that the framing of subordinate legi slation 
is not delayed. The Committee, however, finds that the 
responses from the Ministries/Departments have not been 
prompt in this monitoring exercise undertaken on be half 
of the Committee. 
  
 In view of the above position, the Committee once 
again reiterates its recommendation that the 
Ministries/Departments should ensure putting in pla ce 
subordinate legislation positively within a period of six 
months of coming into force of the Act. The Committ ee 
further recommends that in case the Ministry fails to meet 
with this deadline, they should invariably approach  the 
Committee for seeking extension of time. The Commit tee 
further recommends that in cases where the time lim it of 
six months is not adhered to, they should, while la ying 
rules/regulations before the Parliament invariably lay a 
statement explaining the reasons why the framing of  
rules/regulations was delayed beyond six months so as to 
keep the Parliament apprised of the compliance of t he 
Parliament’s mandate  conferred upon the Executive.” 
(192 
nd 
 Report) 
(Presented on 26 th   August 2011)  
 
  Rules/Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are laid by 
different Ministries on the Table of the House unde r 
various provisions of parent Acts passed by Parliam ent. 
These Rules/ Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are publis hed 
in the official Gazette before being laid on the Table of the 
House. Even after they are laid, it is very difficu lt to get 

access to these Notifications. The Committee recomm ends 
that such Rules/Regulations/Orders, etc. laid on th e Table 
of the House should be invariably uploaded on the 
websites of respective Ministries immediately on th e same 
day when they have been laid on the Table of the Ho use, 
for information of Members of Parliament and people  at 
large for their easy access. 
201 
st  Report 
(Presented on 14 th  December, 2012)  
 
 
The Committee observes that the whole process of 
enacting laws is defeated if rules are not framed a nd laid 
on the Table of the House in time.  A reasonable de lay 
could be understood but unjustifiably long delays s hould 
be avoided and the Ministries should work towards 
improving this position.   The Committee hopes that 
Ministry would strive to keep the delay to the mini mum 
and take care that Notifications are laid on the Ta ble of 
the House at the first available opportunity after 
publication of Notifications. 
 
The Committee would like to impress upon the 
Ministry that it is their responsibility to ensure that copies 
of the Notifications are printed timely and for thi s 
purpose, they need to evolve a suitable mechanism t o 
ensure that notifications are laid in time.   The C ommittee 
is happy that the Ministry has evolved an internal 
mechanism/ procedure for this purpose.  The Committ ee 
hopes that it would take action accordingly in orde r to 
comply with the prescribed schedule in the matter o f 
laying of statutory Notifications. 
 

The Ministry must take appropriate step to 
remove lacuna, if any, administrative or otherwise,  
causing such long delay by being little proactive a nd 
prompt.  Further, the Ministries should take it up with the 
Ministry of Urban Development for late receiving of  
printed copies of the Notification. 
212 th   Report 
(Presented on  3 rd  September, 2013) 
 
 
 “The Committee is not inclined to accept the late 
availability of printed copies of Notifications fro m the 
Government of India Press as the reason for delay i n 
laying of the Notifications. The Committee directs all the 
Ministries that in case there is a delay in procuri ng 
printed copies in time, they may obtain G.S.R. and S.O. 
numbers from the Government of India Press and 
prepare requisite number of copies in cyclostyled form for 
laying in the Parliament. The Committee also 
recommends that this process may be adopted by 
Ministries suo moto  on immediate basis so as to avoid such 
delays henceforth”.
